口径说明：星级是本文按各厂商公开产品文档、计费页所列能力项给出的示意档位，非厂商官方评分；「是／—」按公开能力清单整理，「—」表示未见同口径单独公布，不等于不具备。通义千问这边只列 Qwen-VL 一条，其 Qwen-Audio、Qwen-VL-Max 分别对应语音与视频帧理解，为免表格过长未单列。商汤的音频档来自其语音大模型与按分钟计费的实时多模态 Omni 接口，视频档来自融合模态「图片、文本、视频原生统一」的官方口径；如果需求是纯音频转写而非实时交互，接入前建议先按官方文档确认接口形态。

总结：商汤日日新的着力点在「看懂之后能把活干完」——融合模态原生统一图片、文本、视频，视觉理解结果可以直接进入分析与生成环节；通义千问 Qwen-VL 在纯图文理解上依然很能打；Kimi 专注图文加 PDF 长文档；文心和豆包在图文加语音方向较成熟；GLM-4V 工具调用配合图文理解，适合挂进 Agent 场景。

这张表看着简单，但选型的关键不在「星星多不多」，而在你的场景是「识别」还是「理解」。识别是认出图里有什么字、有什么物体，几乎所有模型都能做；理解是要结合上下文回答「这张图说明了什么问题」，这才拉开差距。比如同样一张服务器监控截图，识别层面大家都能读出数字，但只有做过视觉指令微调的模型才会答出「CPU 使用率异常，可能是某进程死循环」这种带推理的结论。如果你的需求只是 OCR 提取文字，不必上旗舰档，普通档甚至专门的 OCR 接口更便宜也更快；如果需要模型基于图像内容做判断、生成建议、甚至顺着结论产出文档，才值得用旗舰档——这一档再往上，比的就是谁能把多步任务跑完，而不只是单轮答得漂亮。

### 图像理解接入示例

接入结构示意 · 非官方 SDK 示例，端点与字段以官方文档为准

代码语言：javascript

AI代码解释

复制
# 结构示意：把「图 + 指令」发给融合模态模型，拿回结论
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",              # 官网控制台创建
    base_url="https://api.sensenova.cn/v1",    # 结构示意，以官方文档为准
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="SenseNova-V6.5-Pro",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {
                        "url": "https://example.com/diagram.png"   # 或 base64 data URI
                    }
                },
                {
                    "type": "text",
                    "text": "请分析图中的架构图，列出核心组件及其关系。"
                }
            ]
        }
    ],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
这段代码里最容易被忽略的是image_url 到底填 URL 还是 Base64。两种方式各有代价，我列个对比方便你选：

方式

优点

缺点

适用场景

---|---|---|---

URL 引用

请求体小、不占本地内存、便于批量处理

图片必须公网可访问，内网图片要先上传到对象存储

图片本来就有公网地址（如用户上传到 OSS 的头像、商品图）

Base64 内嵌

不依赖外部可访问性，本地文件直接转

请求体膨胀（体积约放大 33%），大图容易撞 payload 上限

本地临时文件、截图、不方便公网暴露的敏感图片

实践中我踩过一个坑：把一张 8MB 的高清截图直接转 Base64 塞进去，结果报400 Bad Request: request entity too large。原因是 Base64 编码后体积膨胀到 10MB 以上，超过了网关允许的请求体上限。解决办法很简单——上传前用 Pillow 把长边压到 1600px 以内再转码，图片里的文字信息基本不丢，但体积能压掉七八成：

截图预处理脚本

代码语言：javascript

AI代码解释

复制
from PIL import Image
import io, base64

def compress_image(path, max_side=1600, quality=85):
    img = Image.open(path).convert("RGB")
    w, h = img.size
    scale = max_side / max(w, h)
    if scale < 1:
        img = img.resize((int(w * scale), int(h * scale)))
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    img.save(buf, format="JPEG", quality=quality)
    return base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()
另一个容易忽略的点是计费：图像也是按 token 折算的，通常做法是按分辨率切成若干个「图块」（tile），每个图块折算成固定 token 数，图片越大、切的图块越多、花的 token 越多。所以不是「分辨率越高效果越好」，超过模型实际有效识别分辨率之后再堆像素，只是在多花钱，识别精度未必有提升。我一般的经验值是：纯文字截图（如报错日志、发票）压到 1200~1600px 长边就够用，人像或复杂场景图可以留到 2000px。

顺带说一层成本差：商汤的融合模态是原生架构，官方口径是长链路场景下 token 消耗比纯文本智能体节约约 60%——这个数字的适用前提是「多步任务」，单张图问答感受不到差别；如果你的场景是一次调用连着读图、检索、写报告，这个折扣才真正算得进来。

### 音频理解接入示例

实时多模态结构示意 · 非官方接口，按分钟计费

代码语言：javascript

AI代码解释

复制
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="SenseNova-V6-Omni",          # 官方计费页：0.2 元/分钟
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "input_audio",
                    "input_audio": {
                        "data": "<base64_encoded_audio>",
                        "format": "wav"        # 支持 mp3/wav/m4a 等
                    }
                },
                {
                    "type": "text",
                    "text": "请转录这段音频，并给出要点摘要。"
                }
            ]
        }
    ],
)
音频这块我提醒你三件事，都是真实踩过的坑：

- format 字段要跟文件实际编码一致，不是跟文件后缀一致。我遇到过一个很迷惑的报错：明明文件叫 voice.wav，接口却返回「解码失败，请检查音频格式」。后来发现是同事用某些录音软件导出的「wav」内部其实是 ADPCM 压缩编码，不是标准 PCM，模型侧解码器识别不出来。排查这类问题最快的办法是本地先用 ffprobe input.wav 看一眼实际编码格式，确认是 PCM / AAC 这些主流编码，不对就转成标准单声道 16kHz PCM 再传。
- 音频文件的大小和时长有隐性上限。官方文档写的「支持 xx 分钟」经常是理想情况，实际网络环境下用 Base64 传超过 5 分钟的音频，请求常常在传输阶段就超时，报的还是通用的timeout，而不是明确的大小超限提示，容易误判成网络问题。稳妥做法是长音频先切片（比如按 60 秒一段），分段调用后再把结果拼接。
- 语音识别类任务不要迷信「模型能听懂方言」。各厂商在这块的实际水平差异很大，普通话标准的场景大家都能打 90 分以上，遇到方言浓重或专业术语密集（比如医疗、法律录音）建议先用小样本测一遍准确率，别直接上生产。实时交互场景还要多算一笔账：按分钟计费的接口（如 Omni 档 0.2 元/分钟）成本跟时长线性相关，跟按 token 计费的图文接口不是一把尺子。

音频预处理：先查编码，再转标准 PCM

代码语言：javascript

AI代码解释

复制
# 1. 看实际编码，不要看后缀
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,sample_rate,channels input.wav

# 2. 转成标准单声道 16kHz PCM
ffmpeg -i input.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 output.wav

# 3. 长音频按 60 秒切片，分段送识别再拼接
ffmpeg -i input.wav -f segment -segment_time 60 -c copy part_%03d.wav

### 价格说明

截至 2026 年 11 月，以各厂商官网公示为准：多模态模型通常比纯文本旗舰档贵一截，图像按「图块折算 token」、音频按「字符数」或「分钟数」叠加计费。商汤这边的公开计费口径是几档并行的：融合模态按 tokens 后付费，SenseNova-V6.5-Pro 输入 0.003 元/千 tokens、输出 0.009 元/千 tokens（折算成每百万 tokens 约 3 元 / 9 元），Turbo 档 0.0015 / 0.0045，Reasoner 档 0.004 / 0.016；按分钟计费的 SenseNova-V6-Omni 是 0.2 元/分钟；图文视觉模型 SenseChat-Vision 为 0.01 / 0.06 元/千 tokens；语音大模型按字符计费，SenseNova-Audio-Fusion 约 3.5 元/万字符。除按量后付费外，还有面向办公场景的 Token Plan 用量套餐（官方口径为平均节省约 60% token 支出）与面向中大型机构的私有化定制方案，前者适合高频团队、后者按业务规模单独报价。

估算成本时不要只看「每张图多少钱」这种宣传口径，实际花费取决于你传的图片分辨率和调用频次。举个例子帮你建立量级感：假设单张图片折算成 500~1000 token（具体数值以官方文档为准，不同分辨率差异很大），一次调用再加上几百字的 prompt 和回复，单次请求的图像部分成本大致是纯文本请求的 3~5 倍。如果你的业务是高频调用（比如工单系统每天几万次截图分析），这笔账要提前打好，尤其要评估是否所有图片都需要上旗舰档识别，还是先用一个轻量分类模型筛出确实需要模型介入的部分，只把这部分转给大模型处理——能省下不少钱。另外提醒一句：单价便宜不等于总价便宜，多步任务里轮次多、上下文长，最终账单主要看总 token 而不是每百万 token 的标价。

### 接入避坑：多模态特有的几个报错

多模态接口比纯文本接口多了几种独有的错误场景，我把遇到过的几个记下来，方便你排查时对号入座：

报错现象：invalid_request_error: image_url is not accessible
这个错误说明模型服务器无法访问你传的图片 URL。常见原因是图片存在内网对象存储里、没开公网读权限，或者 URL 带了签名但签名已过期。排查思路：先在浏览器无痕模式（不带任何登录态）打开这个 URL，能直接看到图片才说明真正公网可读；如果用的是有时效性的签名 URL，注意签名有效期要覆盖模型处理耗时，别刚好卡在边界。

报错现象：调用图像接口偶发 429，但纯文本调用一切正常 多模态接口和纯文本接口经常是分开限流的，即使你的账号纯文本额度充足，图像、音频这类接口可能有单独更低的 QPS 限制（毕竟计算量更大）。遇到这种情况先查官方文档里图像接口单独的限流说明，不要直接套用纯文本的限流数字去做重试退避设计。

报错现象：多图输入时，模型只回答了第一张图，忽略了后面的图 这不是接口 bug，是 prompt 设计问题。多图场景下，如果你在content 里塞了 5 张图却只写一句「分析这些图」，模型经常会偷懒只关注最显眼的一张。解决办法是在文本 prompt 里显式编号，比如「请依次分析图 1、图 2、图 3，分别说明每张图里的问题」，让模型知道要逐一处理，输出质量会明显提升。

报错现象：长音频 / 视频调用超时，报错信息模糊 参考前面音频部分提到的，先切片处理。另外要注意 SDK 的默认超时时间往往是给纯文本对话设的（比如 30 秒），处理音视频这种重计算任务时记得把timeout 参数单独调大，我一般给音频转录接口设到 120 秒起步，避免正常处理还没跑完就被主动掐断连接。

### 常见问题

上传图片的格式和大小有限制吗？ 各厂商限制不同，通常支持 JPEG / PNG / WEBP，单张图片限 10–20 MB，URL 引用或 Base64 均可。超大图片建议先压缩或裁剪后再上传，可减少 token 消耗和延迟。

「原生多模态」和「图文拼接」的模型，用起来差别在哪？ 差别主要体现在多轮、图文交错的任务里。拼接方案通常是视觉编码器接一个文本模型，单张图问答看不出差距，但连续读图、跨图对比、读图后接着写文档这类任务里，图像信息在环节之间容易丢；原生架构是视觉与文本在同一套表征里融合，链路更短。一个实用的判断方法是：给它一份图文混排的多页 PDF，要求「按章节归纳并指出图表支撑了哪个结论」，看它能不能把图里的数字和正文的论断对上，这比看单图问答的准确率更能区分两类模型。

多模态模型能做 OCR 提取表格数据吗？ 可以。商汤的视觉档在 OCRBenchV2 这类视觉评测里成绩靠前，GLM-4V 对表格截图的识别加结构化提取也表现较好。复杂表格（合并单元格、多列）建议在 prompt 中明确要求输出 JSON 或 Markdown 表格格式。实际测试下来，表格越规整（无合并单元格）提取准确率越高，接近 95% 以上；一旦出现合并单元格或者手写体混排，准确率会明显下滑，建议对提取结果做一遍人工校验，别直接入库。

多模态和纯文本模型能不能混用同一套 Key？ 同一厂商下通常可以，账号体系是通的，计费分开算但不需要单独申请。如果你是多厂商混合使用（比如文本用一家、图像用另一家），那就要分别管理两套 Key 和 base_url，建议在项目配置里按「能力类型」而不是「厂商」来组织环境变量，比如TEXT_MODEL_KEY 和 VISION_MODEL_KEY 分开命名，后续换厂商时改动量更小。

该怎么验证自己接入对了？ 最简单的自检方法：拿一张内容确定的图（比如一张写着具体文字的截图）发过去，人工核对返回内容是否准确覆盖了图里的关键信息，而不是泛泛地说「这是一张截图」。如果返回内容对图里细节视而不见，大概率是分辨率压得太狠，或者选错了模型档位（轻量档打不过旗舰档的细粒度识别能力），调整参数重试即可。

### 口径与注意事项

- 表中星级与「是／—」是按各厂商公开产品文档、计费页能力项整理的示意档位，非官方评分；「—」表示该维度未见同口径公开说明，不等于不具备。各厂商的划线方式不同（有的按模型划、有的按接口划），横向比较时请先确认看的是哪一档。
- 商汤的音频能力对外主要以语音大模型（合成、音色复刻）与按分钟计费的实时多模态 Omni 呈现，与「音频转写」这类单点接口并非同一形态；视频能力来自融合模态的官方口径，具体支持的时长、帧率与输入方式以官方文档为准。
- 价格均为官网公示口径的折算或原值，厂商调价频繁（日日新此前有过一轮全线降价），下单前请以计费页为准；Token Plan 的「节省 60%」是厂商公开口径，实际折扣取决于任务链路长度与上下文规模。
- 文中代码为接入结构示意，非官方 SDK 示例，端点路径、鉴权方式、字段名均以官方文档为准；报错信息取自实际调试记录，不同版本可能有差异。
- 本文按能力维度横向对照，条目顺序为阅读顺序，不构成排名或采购建议；选型请结合自身数据合规要求、部署形态与预算自行 POC 验证。

Qwen.content:
# Qwen3.5

Qwen3.5 is a native multimodal large model released by Alibaba Cloud's Tongyi Lab in February 2026, using a hybrid architecture (linear attention + MoE) with 397 billion total parameters and 17 billion activated parameters, supporting 201 languages, and performing excellently in reasoning, programming, agent capabilities, and multimodal understanding.

This document demonstrates how to run this series of models on Radxa AX-M1.:

Model | Parameters | Quantization | Hugging Face Repo 
---|---|---|---
Qwen3.5-0.8B | 0.8B | w8a16 | AXERA-TECH/Qwen3.5-0.8B-AX650-C128-P1152-CTX2047 
Qwen3.5-2B | 2B | w8a16 | AXERA-TECH/Qwen3.5-2B-AX650-C128-P1152-CTX2047 
Qwen3.5-4B | 4B | GPTQ-Int4 | AXERA-TECH/Qwen3.5-4B-AX650-GPTQ-Int4-C128-P1152-CTX2047 

## Install axllm

axllm is an LLM inference tool provided by AXERA, supporting command-line interaction and OpenAI-compatible API.

Method 1: Clone the repo and run the install script
git clone -b axllm https://github.com/AXERA-TECH/ax-llm.git
cd ax-llm
./install.sh

Method 2: One-line install (default branchaxllm)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AXERA-TECH/ax-llm/axllm/install.sh | bash

Method 3: Download executable from GitHub Actions CI

If you don't have a build environment, go to ax-llm Actions to download the latest CI-exported executable:
chmod +x axllm
sudo mv axllm /usr/bin/axllm

## Download Model

### Create virtual environment and install huggingface_hub
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install huggingface_hub

### Download model
hf download AXERA-TECH/Qwen3.5-0.8B-AX650-C128-P1152-CTX2047 --local-dir ./Qwen3.5-0.8B
hf download AXERA-TECH/Qwen3.5-2B-AX650-C128-P1152-CTX2047 --local-dir ./Qwen3.5-2B
hf download AXERA-TECH/Qwen3.5-4B-AX650-GPTQ-Int4-C128-P1152-CTX2047 --local-dir ./Qwen3.5-4B

## Run Model

### Command-line interactive mode
axllm run Qwen3.5-0.8B/
axllm run Qwen3.5-2B/
axllm run Qwen3.5-4B/

VLM Usage Instructions:

- After enteringprompt, you'll see image >>

- Press Enter directly: Text-only conversation
- Enter image path: Image + text conversation
- Entervideo:<frames_dir>: Video/multi-frame conversation

:::tip Usage Tip If you typo and delete when entering the image path, the image path may not be recognized correctly. In this case, enter/reset to reset kvcache and re-enter.
:::
$ axllm run Qwen3.5-0.8B/
...

  /dd        delete one turn  /pp        print historyCtrl+C: stop current generationVLM enabled: after each prompt, input image path (empty = text-only). Use "video:<frames_dir>" for video.

Here are the specific details of the scene:

- **Setting**: They are in a lush green environment. The background is filled with tall trees and vegetation resembling bamboo or palm trees, suggesting a tropical or temperate forest.
- **Atmosphere**: The image creates a sense of mystery and sci-fi adventure. It implies a narrative where space travelers may have landed on Earth to investigate an alien civilization or a lost civilization on Earth.

### OpenAI-compatible API server mode
axllm serve Qwen3.5-0.8B/
axllm serve Qwen3.5-2B/
axllm serve Qwen3.5-4B/

After the server starts, you can call it via HTTP requests:
from openai import OpenAI

API_URL = "http:" + "//127.0.0.1:8000/v1"
MODEL = "Qwen3.5-0.8B"

messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are a helpful assistant."}]},

)

Qwen.content:
# 阿里云Qwen4-Max 大模型详解：定位、特征、能力、适用场景与相对Qwen3-Max差异解析

2026-11-11 65

举报

简介： 2026年11月11日，阿里发布第四代旗舰模型Qwen4-Max预览版，首发千问AI平台Token Plan并接入千问办公、Qoder等入口。该版本聚焦知识理解、世界感知、编程与Agentic四项升级，主打复杂编程、专业办公、前端设计与专业软件操作等真实任务。预览期为11月11日10:00至11月25日24:00，仅支持Token Plan调用，到期后模型标识下线；限时2折、新用户再享5折，最低1折可体验。

刚刚，阿里全新一代大模型Qwen4-Max预览版发布，首发千问AI平台Token Plan。Qwen4模型拥有更强的世界知识和感知能力，并且在编程和Agentic这两项最关键的能力上再度升级，能更好地完成复杂编程、专业办公、前端设计、专业软件操作等真实任务。开发者提前内测的成果显示，Qwen4在3D建模、网页设计、交互等方面展现出亮眼表现。
此次开放的是旗舰模型Qwen4-Max的预览版，Token Plan用户可限时2折、新用户再享折上5折，最低1折即可抢先体验Qwen4模型。同时，千问办公、Qoder、千问APP、QwenStudio等也可第一时间体验。活动详情可参考：https://www.aliyun.com/benefit/scene/tokenplan

## 一、Qwen4-Max 是什么

Qwen4-Max 是阿里云千问（Qwen）系列第四代的旗舰大模型。截至 2026 年 11 月 11 日，官方已发布的是 Qwen4-Max 预览版（模型标识qwen4-max-preview），首发渠道为千问 AI 平台的 Token Plan 订阅服务，同步接入千问办公、Qoder、千问 APP 与 QwenStudio。

### 1.1 基本定位

Qwen4-Max 在千问模型矩阵中处于旗舰位置。按 2026 年 11 月上旬第三方媒体对 Qwen4 家族的梳理，该系列至少规划四款主力模型：Qwen4-Max（性能上限）、Qwen4-Plus（均衡档）、Qwen4-Flash（低成本高速档）、Qwen4-27B（面向本地部署的中等规模档）。Max 代表该家族的能力天花板，定位是复杂任务与专业场景。

阿里云百炼的模型选择文档中，qwen4-max-preview 被归类的适用方向为"复杂推理与编程（Token Plan）"，这与其旗舰定位一致。详情可通过阿里云百炼平台了解：https://www.aliyun.com/product/bailian

### 1.2 当前版本状态：预览版而非正式版

这一点必须准确理解。按千问 AI 平台对模型版本的定义，预览版主要用于新能力验证和收集使用反馈，后续可能持续更新，与面向生产环境的稳定商用版本有所区别。

阿里云百炼 Token Plan 个人版文档给出了明确的预览窗口期：2026 年 11 月 11 日 10:00 至 11 月 25 日 24:00（UTC+8），期间不做变更。

由此可以得出三条实际结论：

- 当前的 Qwen4-Max 是限时可体验的预览版本，不是长期稳定的商用 API；
- 预览期内模型行为不做变更，便于开发者获得一致的测试基准；
- 预览结束后该模型标识会下线，正式版将以新的模型名发布，接入方需要预留改配置的工作量。

对生产环境而言，这意味着预览版适合用于能力评估、场景验证与提前适配，而不适合直接承载不可中断的线上业务。

### 1.3 发布方式的特殊性

Qwen4 的发布路径与常见做法不同。传统路径通常是"开发布会 → 开放 API → 逐步接入应用"，而 Qwen4 采用的是"预览版先进入计费平台与多类应用 → 收集真实调用反馈 → 再发正式版"。

这一节奏变化本身是值得关注的事实：模型能力先进入真实调用场景，通过用户反馈驱动后续迭代。对开发者的直接影响是，可以比过去更早拿到新一代旗舰模型，同时自己踩到的问题与提交的反馈会影响下一个版本。

## 二、模型特征

### 2.1 官方披露的四个能力方向

阿里千问团队在 2026 年 11 月 11 日的官宣中，将 Qwen4 的升级方向概括为三点表述：知识理解更深入、世界感知更立体、Coding 与 Agentic 能力持续进阶。凤凰网科技同日报道进一步归纳为四个方向：知识理解、世界感知、编程能力、智能体能力，并指出覆盖复杂编程、专业办公、前端设计和专业软件操作等任务。

阿里云百炼模型清单中对qwen4-max-preview 标注的能力标签为"模型推理、文本生成、视觉理解"，并标记为 New。这说明该预览版已包含视觉理解能力，而非纯文本模型。

### 2.2 从"问答交互"转向"完成实际任务"

这是本次升级中最具方向性的一点。据阿里方面介绍，相比传统的问答交互，Qwen4 更加注重完成实际任务，能够支持复杂代码编写、前端页面设计、专业办公及软件操作等工作。官方在预告中直接使用了"专为真实任务打造"的表述，并邀请用户"把真实难题交给 Qwen4 试试看"。

这一转向与整个行业的评价体系变化是同向的：衡量标准从"回答得多好"转向"任务完成得多好"，从单轮对话质量转向长链路执行成功率。

### 2.3 架构线索（属于间接信息，需谨慎对待）

关于 Qwen4 的底层架构，目前没有官方直接披露。可参考的间接信息有两条：

- 2026 年 9 月 22 日云栖大会披露：基于下一代架构的 Qwen4 已投入训练，会上展示的 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 仅为 Qwen4 架构的技术预览版，不代表 Qwen4 正式版上线；后续 Qwen4.5、Qwen5 计划将参数规模扩展至 5 万亿至 10 万亿量级。
- 有开发者社区文章称 Qwen4 延续 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 验证的技术路线（稀疏注意力、门控残差、N-gram 嵌入等），重点提升推理效率、降低长上下文算力成本。

上述第二条来自社区与自媒体，未经官方确认，只能作为线索看待。至于网络流传的"百万上下文"等说法，阿里官方页面并未写明，不应作为事实引用。

### 2.4 家族成员的第三方评测表现

在 Qwen4-Max 预览版上线前，第三方评测榜单 GameFeel Bench（一个面向游戏开发场景创造力的垂直基准，考察游戏手感、视觉呈现与创意构思）v1.4 版本中出现了两个未公开型号，业界普遍认为对应 Qwen4 的早期内测版本。据 2026 年 11 月 8 日至 10 日的多家媒体报道：

模型（榜单标识） | GameFeel Bench 得分 | 对照模型得分 | 单次任务成本 
---|---|---|---
Qwen-4-Flash-Early（代号 hawk） | 49.9 | Claude Opus 5.5 (XHigh) 47.2；Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Max) 45.0 | 约 0.40 美元 
Qwen-4-27B-Early | 44.6 | Claude Sonnet 5.5 为 45.0 | 约 0.16 美元 
Claude Opus 5.5（对照） | 47.2 | — | 约 2.60 美元 

需要三点限定：其一，这是第三方垂直榜单，不是通用能力基准；其二，参评的是早期内测版本，不等于正式版或 Max 版；其三，榜单中并未出现 Qwen4-Max 的得分。因此这组数据只能说明 Qwen4 家族在游戏开发类创意任务上具备竞争力，不能用来推断 Qwen4-Max 的具体能力水平。

一个可核查的补充事实：有海外开发者公开分享，仅用一次生成、消耗 69k Tokens，就通过 Java 与 Three.js 完成了一段 3D 渲染，这与官方提到的"3D 建模、网页设计、交互"内测成果方向一致。

## 三、模型能力

以下按能力维度展开，并区分官方定性表述与可验证数据。

### 3.1 知识理解与推理

官方表述为"知识理解更深入"。据媒体归纳，具体指向对专业文献、行业资料与复杂逻辑题的推理能力提升，长文本精读、资料溯源与复杂问题拆解更精准。

可验证数据：尚未公布。 官方未披露 Qwen4-Max 在 GPQA、SuperGPQA、MMLU 等知识类基准上的得分，也未给出与 Qwen3-Max 的对比数值。

作为参照，上一代 Qwen3-Max-Thinking（2026 年 1 月 26 日发布）在启用工具的 HLE（Humanity's Last Exam）评测中得分 58.3，超过 GPT-5.2-Thinking 的 45.5 与 Gemini 3 Pro 的 45.8；在 IMO 难度级别的 IMO-AnswerBench 上得分 91.5。这组数字属于 Qwen3 代际的公开成绩，不代表 Qwen4-Max 的表现。

### 3.2 世界感知与多模态

官方表述为"世界感知更立体"。阿里云百炼模型清单为qwen4-max-preview 标注了"视觉理解"能力标签，说明预览版支持图像输入的理解任务。

据媒体归纳，其优化重点包括图像、图表、截图、文档混合输入的解析，以及图表数据提取、图纸解读、图文混排文档分析。开发者内测反馈集中在 3D 建模、网页设计与交互呈现方面。

### 3.3 编程能力（Coding）

这是本次升级的两个重点之一。官方表述为"Coding 能力持续进阶"，凤凰网科技报道称编程能力是本次升级的重点，可支持复杂代码编写。

具体能力范围据媒体与开发者社区归纳包括：复杂工程代码生成、调试与重构，多文件项目统筹，前端交互页面与全栈项目交付，深层 bug 的定位与修复。内测成果集中体现在 3D 建模、网页设计与交互实现上。

一个可核实的落地信号：Qoder 官方宣布，此前供用户测试的匿名模型 Qoduck 已升级为 Qwen4-Max-Preview，并率先在 Qoder 上线；在此前四天的匿名测试中，Qoduck 每天都更新。此次开放覆盖 Qoder 的全部产品和全部套餐，包括 Teams 与 Enterprise。匿名测试再揭榜的做法，本身构成了对模型编程能力的一种盲测背书。

作为代际参照，上一代 Qwen3.8-Max-0902 版本（2026 年 9 月 2 日升级）在 CodeArena 前端编程总榜以 1691 分登顶，TerminalBench 得分从 11.3 提升至 29.0。Qwen4-Max 在同类榜单上的成绩官方尚未公布。

### 3.4 智能体能力（Agentic）

这是本次升级的另一个重点。官方表述为"Agentic 能力持续进阶"，强调相比传统问答交互更注重完成实际任务，可支持专业办公与专业软件操作。

据媒体与开发者社区归纳，具体指向：长任务拆解、多步骤闭环执行、子智能体调度、工具调用稳定性提升、软件界面操作与跨工具串联任务。

这一方向有明确的前代技术积累。Qwen3-Max-Thinking 已引入自适应工具调用能力，可在对话中自主选择并调用内置的搜索、记忆与代码解释器功能，其训练方式是在工具使用微调后，用基于规则和基于模型的反馈在多样化任务上进一步训练。Qwen4 在此基础上强调"专业软件操作"，意味着智能体的动作空间从"调用 API 类工具"扩展到"操作图形界面软件"。

### 3.5 能力维度的确认状态汇总

---|---|---|---|---

世界感知与多模态 | 世界感知更立体 | 视觉理解 | 未公布 | 支持视觉理解已确认，细节待披露

是否开源 | — | — | 未公布 | 完全未披露 

## 四、适用场景

### 4.1 官方明确指向的四类任务

据 2026 年 11 月 11 日的官方表述与媒体报道，Qwen4-Max 覆盖的任务类型为：复杂编程、专业办公、前端设计、专业软件操作。

### 4.2 按用户角色的场景映射

用户角色 | 典型任务 | 推荐入口 
---|---|---
独立开发者 | 复杂代码项目、批量脚本、Web 全栈开发、深层 bug 修复 | Token Plan（qwen4-max-preview）+ Claude Code / Qwen Code / Cursor 
团队与企业开发 | 多文件工程联动、代码重构、自动化测试、Agent 工作流 | Qoder（含 Teams / Enterprise 套餐） 
前端与设计师 | 网页设计、交互页面实现、3D 建模、可视化呈现 | Qoder、QwenStudio 
办公人群 | 文档撰写与解读、表格处理、资料研读、方案与报告生成 | 千问办公、千问 APP 
智能体开发者 | 提示词调试、Agent 链路测试、工具调用编排、长任务自动化 | QwenStudio、Token Plan API 
企业与科研机构 | 新模型能力评估、场景验证、提前适配 | Token Plan 预览期测试 

### 4.3 不建议使用预览版的场景

基于预览版的版本属性，以下场景应保持谨慎：

- 不可中断的生产业务：预览版将于 2026 年 11 月 25 日 24:00 下线，模型标识会变更，直接上线存在改造风险。
- 对输出稳定性有强一致要求的场景：预览版定位为验证新能力与收集反馈，后续版本可能调整行为。
- 需要长上下文处理的任务：上下文窗口未公布，无法评估是否满足需求。
- 需要私有化部署或开源权重的场景：是否开源尚未披露。
- 有明确合规与 SLA 要求的企业采购：应等待正式商用版本及其服务条款。

## 五、Qwen4-Max-Preview

Qwen4-Max-Preview 是通义千问新一代旗舰多模态模型，于 2026 年 11 月 11 日上线预览。该模型融合文本生成、图片与视频理解及深度思考能力，适用于编程开发、办公、前端设计与复杂智能体任务。

模型能力方面，根据现有文档记录：

- 输入模态：支持文本、图像、视频输入。
- 输出模态：文本输出。
- 推理与思考：属于推理模型，支持深度思考模式。
- 工具调用：支持 Function Calling、联网搜索（web_search）、网页抓取（web_extractor）、代码解释器（code_interpreter）等内置工具。
- 结构化输出：支持 JSON Object 和 JSON Schema 两种结构化输出格式。
- API 兼容性：兼容 OpenAI 与 Anthropic API 协议。

适用场景方面，文档提及该模型适合对推理和理解能力要求更高的任务，具体包括编程开发、办公、前端设计与复杂智能体任务。在模型选型建议中，qwen4-max-preview 被列为"效果优先"选项。

接入与计费限制：当前为预览版，仅支持通过 Token Plan 调用，不支持按量付费或其他计费方式。预览期为 2026 年 11 月 11 日 10:00 至 11 月 25 日 24:00（UTC+8），预览结束后下线。模型 ID 为qwen4-max-preview，别名 qwen4.0-max-preview，两个 ID 均可调用。

## 六、关于 Qwen4-Max 与 Qwen3-Max 的对比

Qwen4-Max 与 Qwen3-Max 的性能对比、基准测试分数或系统性优势分析。可确认以下差异点：

- 多模态能力：qwen4-max-preview 原生支持图像和视频输入；而 Qwen3-Max 系列在部分文档中被归类为"千问Max（思考模式）"且仅在 Chat Completions API / DashScope 下推荐用于思考模式场景，其多模态支持情况需以对应模型文档为准。
- 结构化输出：Qwen4-Max 系列同时支持 JSON Object 和 JSON Schema 结构化输出；Qwen3-Max 系列在部分场景下仅支持非思考模式的结构化输出。
- 上下文与参数规模：现有文档未提供 qwen4-max-preview 的具体上下文长度、参数量等技术规格；Qwen3.8-Max（非 Qwen3-Max）的上下文长度为 100 万 Token、参数量为 2.4 万亿 MoE 架构，但此数据不可直接套用于 Qwen3-Max 或 Qwen4-Max。

### 7.3 优惠与计费口径

模型侧优惠：Qwen4-Max 预览版限时 2 折，新用户在此基础上再享 5 折，叠加后最低为原价的 1 折。Qoder 侧同步给出限时优惠，Credits 消耗倍率为 0.1 倍。此外，千问系列模型在 Token Plan 中普遍适用夜间折扣机制（每日 22:00 至次日 08:00），具体倍率以平台页面为准。

需要明确一点：模型折扣与订阅费是两笔账，不应混算。订阅费决定每月可用的 Credits 总额，模型折扣决定单次调用消耗多少 Credits。

档位 | 月费 | 每月 Credits | 并发 Agent

Essential | 79 元 | 45,000 | 2—3 个

此次调整的幅度为：Lite、Essential、Standard 三档月费不变，月度额度提升约 74%—78%；Pro 档额度由 18 万 Credits 提高至 20 万 Credits，月费由 499 元降至 312 元。调整覆盖存量订阅用户，新额度自 11 月 9 日起陆续生效；Pro 存量用户当前订阅周期价格不变，新价格从下一订阅周期开始执行。

双 11 活动价口径（另行计算）：据阿里云开发者社区 2026 年 11 月 8 日的活动说明，Token Plan 新客首购低至 5 折，Lite 档折算后约 19.5 元/月，活动持续至 11 月 30 日。此口径与上表的日常价属不同价格体系，实际以下单页面为准。

团队版口径：标准席位 198 元/席位/月（限时 150 元），25,000 Credits；高级席位 698 元（限时 550 元），100,000 Credits；尊享席位 1,398 元，250,000 Credits。团队版承诺不使用对话数据训练模型，个人版则数据用于服务改进与模型优化——对数据敏感的企业应选择团队版。

GLM.content:
# Z.ai

Z.ai, formerly Zhipu AI, builds the open-weight GLM family of models for agents, reasoning, and coding.

Z.ai supports Chat Completions requests.

Z.ai is a built-in provider you can pay for with credits, so a provider key is optional. Add your own Z.ai key to bill usage to your Z.ai account instead of your ngrok.ai credits.

## Setup

### Create an access key and add credits
Follow the [quickstart](/ai-gateway/quickstart) to create an access key and purchase [credits](/ai-gateway/concepts/credits) in [app.ngrok.ai](https://app.ngrok.ai).

### Store your Z.ai API key (optional)
Skip this step to pay with credits.
To bring your own key, create an API key in your [Z.ai](https://z.ai/model-api) account. Then [add a provider key](/ai-gateway/guides/attaching-provider-keys#add-a-provider-key) and [create an access key configuration](/ai-gateway/guides/access-key-configurations#create-a-configuration) with a `z-ai` routing rule that uses it.

### Send requests
Send requests with your access key:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://gateway.ngrok.ai/v1",
    api_key="ng-xxxxx-g1-xxxxx",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="z-ai:glm-5.3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)
```

QwenCloud, Tencent TokenHub, and Mistral AI also serve GLM models, so the `z-ai:` prefix keeps the request on Z.ai.

## Available models

See the model catalog.

GLM.title: GLM-5.3 Now Running on SambaCloud
GLM.description: GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's flagship model for complex software engineering and long-horizon agent tasks. ... On Z.ai's internal Code Bench, GLM-5.3 reaches 31.4% at around 50K output tokens per task, ahead of Claude Opus 4.8 at 29.5% with 120K tokens.
GLM.content:
GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's flagship model for complex software engineering and long-horizon agent tasks. It reaches state-of-the-art results among open-weight models on Terminal-Bench 3.0 and Agents' Last Exam, and it does so while using fewer output tokens per task than several closed frontier models. GLM-5.3 is now available on SambaCloud at over 200 tokens/s under the model string GLM-5.3. Read Z.ai's full GLM-5.3 announcement here.

## 
Why GLM-5.3

GLM-5.3 is built for the work that agents actually do: long sequences of dependent steps in a real codebase, terminal, or enterprise system. It scores 28.3 on Terminal-Bench 3.0 and 66.9 on DeepSWE v1.1, state-of-the-art among open-weight models, and it reaches those numbers with fewer output tokens per task than several closed frontier models.

Three things make it a strong fit for teams running agents in production:

- Long-horizon coding and agent work. GLM-5.3 was trained on environments that mirror multi-day expert engineering tasks, with access to compute clusters, codebases, documentation, and experiment results. It is built to own a task end to end rather than wait for a user to decompose it.
- Token efficiency. On Z.ai's internal Code Bench, GLM-5.3 reaches 31.4% at around 50K output tokens per task, ahead of Claude Opus 4.8 at 29.5% with 120K tokens. In agent loops where every step is a model call, fewer tokens per step compounds into lower cost and shorter runs.
- Defensive security. GLM-5.3 holds the best published score on CyberGym, a vulnerability-discovery benchmark, and the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation rated it the most advanced open-weight model for cybersecurity. Teams doing code auditing and vulnerability research get a frontier-class open model for the work.

### Where GLM-5.3 is already running

On OpenRouter, the five apps routing the most tokens to GLM-5.3 are all agent harnesses: Claude Code leads at 2.5T tokens, followed by Hermes Agent (895B), Strix (826B), pi (681B), and omp (476B). Three of those are coding agents, and Strix is an open-source security agent that uses GLM-5.3 to find and validate vulnerabilities. Developers today are not only using GLM-5.3 for chat; they are putting it inside long-running loops where every step is a model call, which is exactly the workload where speed matters most.

Here is a trace from a typical agent run on SambaCloud: 41 model calls over 17 minutes and 30 seconds, 5.4 million input tokens, and just under 42,000 output tokens. Each turn re-sends everything the agent has seen so far, so input grows from 38K tokens on the first call to over 114K by the eighth, while output stays small: a few hundred tokens of reasoning and a tool call. Over 91% of that input was served from cache.

Agentic workloads like this are what GLM-5.3 was trained for, and it is why per-call latency matters more than any single benchmark. Running at over 200 tokens/s on SambaCloud, GLM-5.3 keeps each of those steps short enough that the whole run finishes while the developer is still watching.

## 
Get Started

### Call it from Python

With a few lines of Python, you can hand GLM-5.3 a real engineering task and let it plan, implement, and review its own work.

GLM-5.3 brings frontier agentic coding and the strongest open-weight security capability to production. SambaNova runs it at over 200 tokens/s.

### Try it in ZCode

ZCode is Z.ai's agentic development environment, built for the same long-horizon tasks GLM-5.3 was trained on. It accepts any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible provider, so pointing it at SambaCloud takes four steps:

- Open Settings in the lower-left corner of ZCode and go to Model Providers.
- Add a provider and set the OpenAI Base URL to https://api.sambanova.ai/v1 and the Anthropic Base URL to [SambaCloud Anthropic Messages endpoint].
- Paste your SambaCloud API key.
- Save, then pick GLM-5.3 from the model menu and set reasoning effort to max.

From there ZCode runs GLM-5.3 on SambaCloud for every task: understanding a project, writing code, resolving issues, and multi-step workflows that span hours.

### Other coding agents

The same base-URL swap works in Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex CLI. For Codex, use the Responses API endpoint and declare low, high, and max as the supported reasoning levels in your model catalog.

Try GLM-5.3 in the SambaCloud playground, or generate an API key and connect it to your agent harness today.

# ZhiPu (Z.ai)

ZhiPu AI builds the GLM series of models. Sign up on Z.ai, its global platform. In SuperAgent, ZhiPu uses an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, so it works for Cherry Agent as well as regular chats.

## Get an API Key

- Sign up on Z.ai and create a key on the API Keys page

## Configure in SuperAgent

- Open Model Service Settings and find ZhiPu in the built-in list
- Click Add API key, paste your key, then click Save and close
- If your key comes from Z.ai, replace the API Host with the address given in the Z.ai API documentation; keys from one platform don't work on the other's host
- Click Sync models, add the GLM models you need, and turn on the provider switch in the top-right corner

Some GLM models support built-in web search. See the Z.ai documentation for current models and pricing.

### Get Help and Submit Feedback

If you have any questions, bugs, or feature suggestions during configuration or use, please use the official channels listed in Feedback and Suggestions.

Create an API Key and complete your first Kimi API call.

Kimi API Platform provides access to Kimi K3.1 Pro and other models. You can call these models through Chat Completions API, Responses API, or Messages API.To get started, create an API Key, choose a model, and configure base_url. You can then send requests directly over HTTP or use the OpenAI or Anthropic SDK.

Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are now available. As Kimi’s most capable flagship model to date, K3.1 Pro supports a 1M-token context window and native visual understanding, with significant improvements in coding, 3D creation, financial research, and modeling. It is well suited for programming agents such as Kimi Code, Codex, and Claude Code, as well as knowledge work and deep reasoning. Join the Kimi developer community and let’s build with Kimi!

Visit the Kimi API Platform, sign in, then go to API Keys to create and copy an API Key.Keep your API Key secure. Do not share it with others or hard-code it directly in your application. We recommend storing it in an environment variable:

import osfrom openai import OpenAIclient = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"], base_url="https://api.moonshot.ai/v1",)completion = client.chat.completions.create( model="kimi-k3.1-pro", messages=[ {"role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi, an AI assistant provided by Moonshot AI. You are especially good at conversations in Chinese and English. You provide users with safe, helpful, and accurate answers. You also refuse to answer any questions involving terrorism, racism, pornography, violence, or similar harmful content. Moonshot AI is a proper noun and must not be translated into other languages."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Hi, my name is Li Lei. What is 1+1?"} ])print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

curl https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro", "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi, an AI assistant provided by Moonshot AI. You are especially good at conversations in Chinese and English. You provide users with safe, helpful, and accurate answers. You also refuse to answer any questions involving terrorism, racism, pornography, violence, or similar harmful content. Moonshot AI is a proper noun and must not be translated into other languages."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Hi, my name is Li Lei. What is 1+1?"} ] }'

const OpenAI = require("openai");const client = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.MOONSHOT_API_KEY, baseURL: "https://api.moonshot.ai/v1",});async function main() { const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: "kimi-k3.1-pro", messages: [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi, an AI assistant provided by Moonshot AI. What is 1+1?"} ] }); console.log(completion.choices[0].message.content);}main();

If the code runs successfully without errors, you will see output similar to:

Hello, Li Lei! 1+1 equals 2. This is a basic arithmetic question. If you have any other questions or need help, feel free to let me know.

Note: Because Kimi models are nondeterministic, the actual response may not exactly match the example above.

The examples on this page use the latest model kimi-k3.1-pro by default. K3.1 Pro configures reasoning effort with the top-level reasoning_effort request field (supports "low" / "high" / "max", default "max"). To use another model such as kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed, replace the model field and adjust the parameter configuration for that model. See the Model Parameter Reference.

Kimi.content:
Thinking models use reasoning tokens to “think” before producing a final answer — breaking down the problem, planning steps, and evaluating alternatives. The reasoning process is returned in the response’s reasoning_content field. Thinking before answering improves performance on complex reasoning, code generation, and multi-step tool calling, at the cost of higher latency and token usage.

kimi-k3.1-pro: the flagship thinking model; reasoning and Preserved Thinking are always on, and reasoning_content may be returned. Configure its reasoning effort with the top-level reasoning_effort request field, which supports "low" / "high" / "max" (default "max").

kimi-k3: supports a 1M-token context window and follows the same thinking behavior as K3.1 Pro.

kimi-k3.1-pro always reasons with Preserved Thinking always on; you do not need to (and should not) pass the thinking parameter — just set model, and optionally adjust reasoning effort with the top-level reasoning_effort field:

curl

python

$ curl https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational." } ] }'

import osfrom openai import OpenAIclient = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"], base_url="https://api.moonshot.ai/v1",)completion = client.chat.completions.create( model="kimi-k3.1-pro", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational."}],)message = completion.choices[0].messageif hasattr(message, "reasoning_content"): print(getattr(message, "reasoning_content"))print(message.content)

For multi-turn conversations and tool calls, pass the complete assistant message returned by the API back to messages as-is (including reasoning_content); see Preserved Thinking. For more K3.1 Pro usage, see the Kimi K3.1 Pro Quickstart.

K3.1 Pro: adjust reasoning effort with reasoning_effort

kimi-k3.1-pro always reasons and does not support the thinking parameter. Adjust reasoning effort with the top-level reasoning_effort field ("low" / "high" / "max", default "max"); see Reasoning Effort for usage and examples.

When using a thinking model with thinking enabled, the API response carries the model’s reasoning in the reasoning_content field. When reading this field:

In the OpenAI SDK, ChoiceDelta and ChatCompletionMessage types do not provide a reasoning_content field directly, so you cannot access it via .reasoning_content. You must use hasattr(obj, "reasoning_content") to check if the field exists, and if so, use getattr(obj, "reasoning_content") to retrieve its value.

If you use other frameworks or directly interface with the HTTP API, you can directly obtain the reasoning_content field at the same level as the content field.

In streaming output (stream=True), the reasoning_content field will always appear before the content field. In your business logic, you can detect if the content field has been output to determine if the reasoning (inference process) is finished.

Tokens in reasoning_content are also controlled by the max_tokens parameter: the sum of tokens in reasoning_content and content must be less than or equal to max_tokens.

Thinking models can perform deep reasoning across multiple tool calls to tackle complex tasks. To get reliable results, always follow these configuration rules when using thinking models:

In both single-task tool-call loops and multi-turn conversations, pass the complete assistant message back as-is, including reasoning_content. kimi-k3.1-pro and kimi-k3 always enable Preserved Thinking.

Set max_tokens >= 16000 to ensure the full reasoning_content and content can be returned without truncation.

Do not set temperature.kimi-k3.1-pro and kimi-k3 fix temperature at 1.0; do not pass it explicitly (see Model Parameter Reference).

Enable streaming (stream=True). Because thinking models return both reasoning_content and regular content, the response is larger than usual. Streaming delivers a better user experience and helps avoid network-timeout issues.

The example below demonstrates a “Daily News Report Generation” scenario. The model will sequentially call official tools like date (to get the date) and web_search (to search today’s news), and will present deep reasoning throughout this process:

import osimport jsonimport httpximport openaiclass FormulaChatClient: def __init__(self, base_url: str, api_key: str): """Initialize Formula client""" self.base_url = base_url self.api_key = api_key self.openai = openai.Client( base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key, ) self.httpx = httpx.Client( base_url=base_url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"}, timeout=30.0, ) # Use kimi-k3.1-pro; reasoning and Preserved Thinking are always enabled self.model = "kimi-k3.1-pro" def get_tools(self, formula_uri: str): """Get tool definitions from Formula API""" response = self.httpx.get(f"/formulas/{formula_uri}/tools") response.raise_for_status() try: return response.json().get("tools", []) except json.JSONDecodeError as e: print(f"Error: Unable to parse JSON (status code: {response.status_code})") print(f"Response content: {response.text[:500]}") raise def call_tool(self, formula_uri: str, function: str, args: dict): """Call an official tool""" response = self.httpx.post( f"/formulas/{formula_uri}/fibers", json={"name": function, "arguments": json.dumps(args)}, ) response.raise_for_status() fiber = response.json() if fiber.get("status", "") == "succeeded": return fiber["context"].get("output") or fiber["context"].get("encrypted_output") if "error" in fiber: return f"Error: {fiber['error']}" if "error" in fiber.get("context", {}): return f"Error: {fiber['context']['error']}" return "Error: Unknown error" def close(self): """Close the client connection""" self.httpx.close()# Initialize clientbase_url = os.getenv("MOONSHOT_BASE_URL", "https://api.moonshot.ai/v1")api_key = os.getenv("MOONSHOT_API_KEY")if not api_key: raise ValueError("MOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable not set. Please set your API key.")print(f"Base URL: {base_url}")print(f"API Key: {api_key[:10]}...{api_key[-10:] if len(api_key) > 20 else api_key}\n")client = FormulaChatClient(base_url, api_key)# Define the official tool Formula URIs to useformula_uris = [ "moonshot/date:latest", "moonshot/web-search:latest"]# Load all tool definitions and build mappingprint("Loading official tools...")all_tools = []tool_to_uri = {} # function.name -> formula_urifor uri in formula_uris: try: tools = client.get_tools(uri) for tool in tools: func = tool.get("function") if func: func_name = func.get("name") if func_name: tool_to_uri[func_name] = uri all_tools.append(tool) print(f" Loaded tool: {func_name} from {uri}") except Exception as e: print(f" Warning: Failed to load tool {uri}: {e}") continueprint(f"Loaded {len(all_tools)} tools in total\n")if not all_tools: raise ValueError("No tools loaded. Please check API key and network connection.")# Initialize message listmessages = [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi, a professional news analyst. You excel at collecting, analyzing, and organizing information to generate high-quality news reports.", },]# User request to generate today's news reportuser_request = "Please help me generate a daily news report including important technology, economy, and society news."messages.append({ "role": "user", "content": user_request})print(f"User request: {user_request}\n")# Begin multi-step conversation loopmax_iterations = 10 # Prevent infinite loopsfor iteration in range(max_iterations): try: completion = client.openai.chat.completions.create( model=client.model, messages=messages, max_tokens=1024 * 32, tools=all_tools, ) except openai.AuthenticationError as e: print(f"Authentication error: {e}") print("Please check if the API key is correct and has the required permissions") raise except Exception as e: print(f"Error while calling the model: {e}") raise # Get response message = completion.choices[0].message # Print reasoning process if hasattr(message, "reasoning_content"): print(f"=============Reasoning round {iteration + 1} starts=============") reasoning = getattr(message, "reasoning_content") if reasoning: print(reasoning[:500] + "..." if len(reasoning) > 500 else reasoning) print(f"=============Reasoning round {iteration + 1} ends=============\n") # Add assistant message to context (preserve reasoning_content) messages.append(message) # If the model did not call any tools, conversation is done if not message.tool_calls: print("=============Final Answer=============") print(message.content) break # Handle tool calls print(f"The model decided to call {len(message.tool_calls)} tool(s):\n") for tool_call in message.tool_calls: func_name = tool_call.function.name args = json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments) print(f"Calling tool: {func_name}") print(f"Arguments: {json.dumps(args, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)}") # Get corresponding formula_uri formula_uri = tool_to_uri.get(func_name) if not formula_uri: print(f"Error: Could not find Formula URI for tool {func_name}") continue # Call the tool result = client.call_tool(formula_uri, func_name, args) # Print result (truncate if too long) if len(str(result)) > 200: print(f"Tool result: {str(result)[:200]}...\n") else: print(f"Tool result: {result}\n") # Add tool result to message list tool_message = { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tool_call.id, "name": func_name, "content": result } messages.append(tool_message)print("\nConversation completed!")# Cleanupclient.close()

This process demonstrates how thinking models use deep reasoning to plan and execute complex multi-step tasks when thinking is enabled. Detailed reasoning steps (reasoning_content) are preserved in the context to ensure accurate tool use at every stage.

Kimi.content:
# Moonshot Kimi

Source: https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/models/moonshot-kimi

Use Moonshot Kimi models for reasoning, chat, and coding through Runpod Public Endpoints, with supported inputs, outputs, and request examples.

Moonshot's Kimi family of models handles advanced reasoning and chat. It supports extended thinking with a visible reasoning trace before the final answer. A single endpoint serves five variants, each selected by setting themodel field in the request body.

[card] Try in playground

Test Moonshot Kimi in the Runpod Hub playground.

Endpoint | https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/runsync 
---|---
Pricing | $4.00-$20.00 per 1M output tokens, $0.95-$4.00 per 1M input tokens 
Type | Text generation 

[!NOTE]

This endpoint is fully compatible with the OpenAI API. See the OpenAI compatibility examples below.

## Model variants

Choose a variant by setting themodel field in the request body (default kimi-k2.6). The endpoint slug stays moonshot-kimi for every variant.

model value | Description | Context window | Input price | Output price 
---|---|---|---|---
kimi-k2.6 (default) | General-purpose model with thinking and non-thinking modes, agentic capabilities, and multimodal input. | 256K (262,144 tokens) | $0.95 per 1M tokens | $4.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k2.7-code | Coding-focused model with thinking mode and agentic capabilities. | 256K (262,144 tokens) | $0.95 per 1M tokens | $4.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k3 | Flagship model with always-on reasoning and configurable reasoning effort for long-horizon coding and knowledge work. | 1M (1,048,576 tokens) | $3.00 per 1M tokens | $15.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k3.1-pro | Moonshot's 3T-class open-weight model with always-on reasoning, for long-horizon coding and agentic work. | 1M | $2.00 per 1M tokens | $10.00 per 1M tokens 
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed | Kimi K3.1 Pro served for higher throughput, for interactive coding and agent loops. | 1M | $4.00 per 1M tokens | $20.00 per 1M tokens 

To target a variant other than the default, set themodel field to its ID. For example, to use the flagship model, set "model": "kimi-k3" in the request body (or model="kimi-k3" with the OpenAI SDK).

## Request

All parameters are passed within theinput object in the request body.

input.messagesarray required

Array of message objects with role and content.

input.messages[].rolestring required

The role of the message author. Usesystem, user, or assistant.

input.messages[].contentstring required

The content of the message.

input.modelstring (default: kimi-k2.6)

The Kimi variant to use. One ofkimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k3, kimi-k3.1-pro, or kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed.

input.sampling_params.max_tokensinteger (default: 2048)

Maximum number of tokens to generate. Kimi K3.1 models reason before they answer, and reasoning tokens count toward this limit. For coding tasks withkimi-k3.1-pro or kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed, set it to 8,192 or higher so the model has room to finish its answer.

input.sampling_params.temperaturefloat (default: 1)

Controls randomness in generation. Lower values make output more deterministic.

input.sampling_params.seedinteger

Seed for reproducible results.

input.sampling_params.top_kinteger

Restricts sampling to the top K most probable tokens.

input.sampling_params.top_pfloat

Nucleus sampling threshold. Range: 0.0-1.0.
curl -X POST "https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/runsync" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNPOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "input": {
      "messages": [
        {
          "role": "system",
          "content": "You are Kimi."
        },
        {
          "role": "user",
          "content": "What is Runpod?"
        }
      ],
      "sampling_params": {
        "max_tokens": 2048,
        "temperature": 1
      },
      "model": "kimi-k2.6"
    }
  }'
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/runsync",
    headers={
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {RUNPOD_API_KEY}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    json={
        "input": {
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi."},
                {"role": "user", "content": "What is Runpod?"},
            ],
            "sampling_params": {
                "max_tokens": 2048,
                "temperature": 1,
            },
            "model": "kimi-k2.6",
        }
    },
)

result = response.json()
print(result["output"])
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/runsync",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${RUNPOD_API_KEY}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      input: {
        messages: [
          { role: "system", content: "You are Kimi." },
          { role: "user", content: "What is Runpod?" },
        ],
        sampling_params: {
          max_tokens: 2048,
          temperature: 1,
        },
        model: "kimi-k2.6",
      },
    }),
  }
);

const result = await response.json();
console.log(result.output);

## Response

idstring

Unique identifier for the request.

statusstring

Request status. ReturnsCOMPLETED on success, FAILED on error.

delayTimeinteger

Time in milliseconds the request spent in queue before processing began.

executionTimeinteger

Time in milliseconds the model took to generate the response.

workerIdstring

Identifier of the worker that processed the request.

outputobject

The generation result containing the text and usage information.

output.choicesarray

Array containing the generated text.

output.costfloat

Cost of the generation in USD.

output.usageobject

Token usage information.
{
  "id": "sync-a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890-u1",
  "status": "COMPLETED",
  "delayTime": 15,
  "executionTime": 2345,
  "workerId": "oqk7ao1uomckye",
  "output": {
    "choices": [
      {
        "tokens": [
          "Runpod is a cloud computing platform that provides GPU resources for AI and machine learning workloads..."
        ]
      }
    ],
    "cost": 0.00074,
    "usage": {
      "input": 35,
      "output": 150
    }
  }
}
{
  "id": "sync-a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890-u1",
  "status": "FAILED",
  "error": "Invalid messages format"
}

## OpenAI API compatibility

Moonshot Kimi is fully compatible with the OpenAI API format. You can use the OpenAI Python client to interact with this endpoint. You can setmodel to any of the five variant IDs.
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=RUNPOD_API_KEY,
    base_url="https://api.runpod.ai/v2/moonshot-kimi/openai/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "system",
            "content": "You are Kimi.",
        },
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "What is Runpod?",
        },
    ],
    max_tokens=2048,
    temperature=1,
    reasoning_effort="max", # set for adding reasoning
    top_p=0.9,
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)

For streaming responses, addstream=True:
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k2.6",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in simple terms."}
    ],
    max_tokens=2048,
    stream=True,
)

for chunk in response:
    if chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
        print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="")

For more details, see Send vLLM requests and the OpenAI API compatibility guide.

## Cost calculation

Moonshot Kimi charges separate rates for input and output tokens, and the rate depends on the variant. Kimi K2.6 and Kimi K2.7 Code charge $0.95 per 1M input tokens and $4.00 per 1M output tokens. Kimi K3 charges $3.00 per 1M input tokens and $15.00 per 1M output tokens. Kimi K3.1 Pro charges $2.00 per 1M input tokens and $10.00 per 1M output tokens, and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed charges $4.00 per 1M input tokens and $20.00 per 1M output tokens. Example costs:

Tokens | K2.6 & K2.7 Code input ($0.95/1M) | K2.6 & K2.7 Code output ($4.00/1M) | K3 input ($3.00/1M) | K3 output ($15.00/1M) 
---|---|---|---|---
1,000 tokens | $0.00095 | $0.004 | $0.003 | $0.015 
10,000 tokens | $0.0095 | $0.04 | $0.03 | $0.15 
100,000 tokens | $0.095 | $0.40 | $0.30 | $1.50 
1,000,000 tokens | $0.95 | $4.00 | $3.00 | $15.00

# Grok 4.7

## xAI — Grok 4.7

## Model Details

Grok 4.7 is xAI's frontier model, built for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, with support for text and image input. It builds on previous generations of Grok with a focus on long-running agents and more ambitious interactive work. It offers a 524,288-token context window shared between input and output, and configurable reasoning efforts (low, medium, high, xhigh).

- Model launch date: September 28, 2026
- EOL no sooner than: September 28, 2027
- Legacy period: at least 6 months
- Model lifecycle policy: Model lifecycle
- Model EOL date: N/A
- End User License Agreements and Terms of Use: View
- Model lifecycle: Active
- Context window: 524,288 tokens, shared between input and output
- Max output tokens: 524,288 minus input tokens
- Reasoning: Supported (configurable: low, medium, high, xhigh)

xAI.content:
#### Use Grok Bot

# Grok Bot for Mobile

Use Grok Bot on iPhone or Android to start work, answer questions, approve steps, and review results away from your desk.

The mobile app connects to the same Bots, conversations, routines, connectors, and shared cloud computer as the desktop app. Work continues in the cloud when the app is closed.

## Requirements

- iPhone with iOS 18 or later, or a phone with Android 9 or later
- An eligible plan: Premium, Super, or Ultra on The X Subscription, for an individual or a team seat. On a legacy Cursor plan, every paid individual plan and Cursor Teams include Grok Bot, and you can also link an individual SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy, or X Premium+ subscription. See Grok Bot on The X Subscription and Plans and billing.
- Internet connection

The iOS app also runs on iPad (iPadOS 18 or later).

Download Grok Bot from the App Store on iPhone or Google Play on Android.

## Sign in and set up

- Open Grok Bot.
- On iPhone, choose Continue with Google, Sign in with Apple, or Continue with email. If you're signed in to the X app or the Grok app on the same iPhone, Grok Bot can offer Continue as that account instead; choose Other options to see the rest. On Android, choose Log In or Sign Up and complete sign-in in the browser.
- Use the same account you use on desktop or web. If your account asks for a code from an authenticator app, enter it on the Enter your verification code screen, or choose Use the browser instead.
- Return to the app. If your access comes from a SuperGrok or X Premium+ subscription, choose Link Grok Account when the access screen asks, finish signing in to Grok in the browser, then choose Finished Linking? Refresh My Status. A link made on desktop or the web also works on the phone with the same Cursor account.

New users can complete the first-run tour, choose a first Bot, and wait while the shared computer is set up. Existing users go directly to their synced Bot list.

Enable notifications if you want to know when a Bot has a result, question, or approval request. While you use the desktop app on macOS or Windows, notifications from Bots you own go to the desktop instead; see Control notifications for when your phone is still notified.

There is no setting that keeps your phone quiet only while the desktop app is open. To stop alerts for one Bot, tap the Bot's name at the top of its chat and turn off Notifications; the note there is Get notified when this Bot finishes or is waiting for you. Off means that Bot does not notify you, including on your phone. On desktop, ask the Bot to turn its notifications off. To stop phone alerts for every Bot, open Settings on the phone and turn off Notifications. If the phone says Notifications are off, choose Open Settings and allow notifications for Grok Bot there only if you want them back.

## Access and subscriptions

Grok Bot access carries into mobile when you sign in with the same Cursor account. This includes:

- Premium, Super, or Ultra on The X Subscription, including team seats
- Legacy Cursor Ultra, Cursor Pro+, or Cursor Pro
- Legacy Cursor Teams (self-serve) seats
- SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, or SuperGrok Heavy account links
- X Premium+ account links

You should not buy a second subscription through Apple or Google Play in these cases. You can still upgrade within your plans, such as Pro+ to Ultra. A Cursor plan and a SuperGrok or X Premium+ link do not add together; Grok Bot uses whichever one grants more weekly usage. Your phone and desktop share the same usage on your Cursor account.

### Subscribe from the phone

If your Cursor account doesn't already include Grok Bot, subscribe from the mobile app:

- Open Grok Bot on your phone.
- Choose a plan on the paywall screen.
- Complete the in-app purchase through the App Store on iOS or Google Play on Android.

Only monthly individual plans are available through the mobile app. For yearly billing, Teams, or Enterprise plans, subscribe on cursor.com. If you subscribed in the app and want on-demand usage, enable it on the web.

### Manage or cancel a phone subscription

The store you bought through handles the subscription, including store free trials (intro offers). Cursor can't cancel an in-app plan or refund it for you.

- iOS: Apple handles in-app subscriptions. Cancel or change the plan in Apple ID → Subscriptions before a trial ends if you do not want it to convert to a paid subscription. For Apple billing questions and refunds, use Apple's subscription support.
- Android: Google Play handles in-app subscriptions. Cancel or change the plan in the Google Play app under Payments & subscriptions → Subscriptions. For Google Play billing questions and refunds, use Google Play's refund support. Android has no in-app trial. A Google Play subscription belongs to the Grok Bot account that bought it. If it was bought while you were signed in to a different Grok Bot account, changing the plan from the app fails with a general error and nothing is charged. Sign in to the account that owns the subscription to change the plan, or let it end and subscribe again from the account you want to use.

The Grok Bot usage-credit trial claimed on web or desktop is separate; see Is there a free trial?.

### Use a usage limit reset

A usage limit reset brings your weekly usage back to 0% right away, without waiting for your regular weekly reset. Resets you have are listed under Usage limit resets in Settings > Usage, with the date each one expires. Tap Usage Limit Reset, then Confirm. After you use one, you have to wait before you can use another.

When you reach your weekly usage limit, the warning above the message box also offers Use reset. It isn't offered before you reach the limit, because using a reset early gives up the usage you have left that week.

If you have no resets and can refer friends, Usage limit resets shows No resets available. Tap it to refer a friend for a free usage reset.

## Message a Bot

From a conversation, you can:

- Send text
- Dictate a message with Start dictation
- Start a voice chat with Start voice chat
- Play a voice memo a Bot sent
- Take or attach a photo
- Choose an image or file
- Mention another Bot or@everyone in a group
- Reply in a thread
- React to a message

Drafts are saved per conversation when you navigate away.

Touch and hold a message and choose Select Text to select its text in place. Adjust the selection, then choose Add to Chat to quote it in your reply, or copy it.

To send something from another app, use the system share sheet and choose Grok Bot. You can share a photo, file, link, or text on iPhone, and text, photos, videos, audio, or PDFs on Android. Grok Bot sends it without leaving the app you're in: your primary Bot, if you have one, starts in To:, or pick another Bot from the list or search for one. Optionally Add a note, then choose Send. If the share can't be sent from there, choose Open in Grok Bot to finish in the app.

Choose Start voice chat when the composer is empty to talk with the Bot live. While you are on the line, a Voice chat control stays under the header. See Message and collaborate.

When a Bot prepares an email or Slack message, the conversation can show a draft you can edit. Choose Send or Discard.

## Use Siri, Shortcuts, and Live Activities on iPhone

Grok Bot adds shortcuts you can run from Siri, Spotlight, or the Shortcuts app: List Bots, Send Message, Start Dictation, and Start Voice Chat. For example, say "Send a message in Grok Bot."

Start Dictation lets you dictate a message to a Bot without opening the app, as long as your iPhone is unlocked. While it runs, a Live Activity on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island shows its progress, with buttons to cancel or send. A voice chat also shows a Live Activity while you're on the line.

On an iPhone with an Action Button, you can press it to talk with a Bot. In your iPhone's Settings, choose Action Button, swipe to Shortcut, and choose Grok Bot > Start Voice Chat. If you don't pick a Bot for the shortcut, Grok Bot asks which one. Press it again while you're on the line to hang up.

## Create Bots and groups

Use the + control on the home screen to choose New Bot or New Group Chat. You can also edit a Bot profile, manage group members, pin or hide a conversation, and delete a Bot.

## Review the computer

Open the computer from a conversation when you need to:

- Watch browser or desktop work
- Take over for a password, two-factor code, or CAPTCHA
- Inspect the current screen
- Hand control back with I'm done

The screen is the same shared computer used by every Bot on your account.

Updating and recovering the computer aren't available on mobile. Use desktop Grok Bot to update or recover it, or to reconnect your phone when the computer won't connect; see The computer cannot be reached.

## Let a Bot use your phone's apps

A Bot can use some apps on your phone when you ask, such as checking your calendar or setting a timer. This works only in your own chat with a Bot you own in the Grok Bot app. It doesn't work in group chats, in other apps such as Slack, or with a Team Bot someone else owns.

On iPhone and Android:

- Calendar: read your events, and add, change, or delete them. New events go in your default calendar unless you name another one. The Bot can't change or delete a repeating event, and it never invites anyone.
- Contacts: look someone up by name for a phone number, email, address, or birthday, or list your contacts when you ask to see them. The Bot only reads your contacts. If you shared only some contacts with Grok Bot, it sees only those.
- Location: read where your phone is right now. The Bot gets a position, not an address or place name, and how precise it is depends on your phone's location settings.
- Alarms: set an alarm or start a timer. An alarm rings once, the next time your phone's clock shows that time, so it can't be set more than 24 hours ahead. A timer runs for up to 24 hours. The Bot can't change

# Elon Musk announces Grok 4.8 featuring a full C++ stack rewrite: what to know

The engineering team has completely abandoned JAX and SGLang to write a bare-metal C/C++ stack for RL and inference

Published November 10, 2026

Elon Musk has announced Grok 4.8 stating that the AI model has been completely re-engineered in C++ in its newest version. Pre-training for Grok 4.8 was completed after cleaning supervised fine-tuning data and now experiencing a positive feedback loop.

A soft rollout will hit Grok Bot users later this week, promising no similarity to version 4.7 and a stronger architecture for future growth. Users have already spotted advances like reduced resource consumption after resets, alongside recent upgrades such as individual bot tracking, an educational hub featuring AI programs and upcoming iMessage compatibility.

The 55-year-old posted on social platform X, “We have dumped JAX/SGLang and rewritten the entire RL and inference stack from scratch in C/C++, which took some extra time.”

“Training (aka pre-training) is done. A lot of cleanup was needed on the SFT data to get that mostly right. Now, 4.8 is in RL and the evals are starting to climb. We will do a soft rollout to Bot users later this week and see how it goes.”

On social platform X, users have been responding with one writing, “I don’t think people understand what it means to create something in the complexity of grok with your own C headers without using other libraries. This is insane work.”

Second added, “At least it was nice how Grok precisely calculated the Doppler effect on my satellite radio frequencies in a 500-km orbit. He must have had good training.”

Ruqia Shahid is a reporter specialising in science, focusing on discoveries, research developments, and technological advancements. She translates complex scientific concepts into clear, engaging stories, helping readers understand the latest innovations and their real-world impact through accurate, accessible, and insight-driven reporting.

xAI.content:
# xAI (Grok)

Thexai provider supports xAI's Grok models through an API interface compatible with OpenAI's format, including text, vision, image generation, video generation, and voice workflows.

## Setup

To use xAI's API, set theXAI_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file.
export XAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

When xAI is the selected fallback provider family, Promptfoo can use xAI defaults for grading, suggestions, synthesis, and web search. These automatic defaults currently usegrok-4.3 on the global endpoint; select grok-4.7, grok-4.6, or grok-4.5 explicitly where they are available. xAI does not currently expose a public embeddings or moderation API, so those defaults fall back to OpenAI when xAI is selected. Explicit provider IDs in your config still take precedence.

## Supported Models

The xAI provider includes support for the following model formats. xAI recommendsgrok-4.7 for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work; consult the public model catalog for current availability.

Legacy xAI model aliases

xAI periodically retires older model slugs and keeps them working through redirects. As of the May 15, 2026 (12:00 PM PT) retirement, requests to thegrok-4-1-fast, grok-4-fast, grok-4-0709, and grok-3 families redirect to grok-4.3 and use Grok 4.3 pricing. Requests to grok-code-fast-1 route to grok-build-0.1, while grok-imagine-image-pro routes to grok-imagine-image-quality. For new configs, use a current canonical model ID directly.

Regional model availability

xAI documents Grok 4.7 on its global and US regional endpoints, and announced Grok 4.5 availability in the EU API Console. Check your account before depending on Grok 4.7 in another region;grok-4.3 remains Promptfoo's automatic fallback.

### Grok 4.7 Models

- xai:grok-4.7 - Chat Completions; 500K context, text and image input, text output
- xai:responses:grok-4.7 - Responses API, including server-side tools and encrypted reasoning

Use the exactgrok-4.7 model ID. Grok 4.7 Fast is available in Cursor and Grok Build, but not on the public xAI API.

### Grok 4.6 Models

- xai:grok-4.6 - Previous flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)

xAI does not publish any aliases for this model, so target the exactgrok-4.6 id. There is no grok-4.6-latest.

### Grok 4.5 Models

- xai:grok-4.5 - Flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)
- xai:grok-4.5-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family
- xai:grok-build-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.5 family

### Grok 4.3 Models

- xai:grok-4.3 - General-purpose reasoning model
- xai:grok-4.3-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.3 family
- xai:grok-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.3 family

### Grok 4.20 Models

- xai:grok-4.20-0309-reasoning - Reasoning model
- xai:grok-4.20 - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-reasoning - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-reasoning-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning - Non-reasoning variant
- xai:grok-4.20-non-reasoning - Alias for the Grok 4.20 non-reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-non-reasoning-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 non-reasoning family
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 - Multi-agent variant
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family
- xai:grok-4.20-multi-agent-latest - Alias for the Grok 4.20 multi-agent family

### Grok 4.1 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-1-fast-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning and its -latest aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok Code Fast Models

- xai:grok-build-0.1 - Canonical Grok Build coding model (256K context)
- xai:grok-code-fast-1 - Legacy alias that routes to grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast - Alias for grok-build-0.1
- xai:grok-code-fast-1-0825 - Versioned alias for grok-build-0.1

### Grok-4 Fast Models

These legacy IDs remain recognized for backward compatibility and redirect to Grok 4.3:

- xai:grok-4-fast-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with low reasoning effort
- xai:grok-4-fast-non-reasoning and its aliases - Redirect with reasoning disabled

### Grok-4 Models

- xai:grok-4-0709, xai:grok-4, and xai:grok-4-latest - Legacy IDs that redirect to Grok 4.3 with low reasoning effort

### Grok-3 Models

Thegrok-3, grok-3-beta, grok-3-fast, and related -latest IDs are legacy aliases that redirect to Grok 4.3. Promptfoo also recognizes the older Grok 3 Mini IDs for backward compatibility; verify their availability for your xAI account before relying on them.

### Grok-2 and previous Models

Promptfoo recognizes oldergrok-2, grok-beta, and vision IDs for existing configs, but they are not in xAI's current public catalog. Use a current model for new configs and verify legacy availability in the xAI Console.

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI-compatible configuration options plus Grok-specific options, subject to the model restrictions below. Example usage:

When xAI returnsusage.cost_in_usd_ticks, Promptfoo uses that exact billed amount, including cache discounts and request-level pricing adjustments. If ticks are unavailable, Promptfoo falls back to the model's catalog rates and applies the documented 2x premium when the response confirms service_tier: priority. Custom pricing can be set with cost, inputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost (all per-token rates); explicit overrides take precedence over reported ticks and are used as final rates without an additional priority multiplier.
providers:
  - id: xai:grok-4.7
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      reasoning_effort: 'xhigh' # low, medium, high (default), or xhigh
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to XAI_API_KEY

Bothxai:<model> Chat Completions and xai:responses:<model> support xAI
Priority Processing.
Set service_tier to priority for higher scheduling priority or default for standard
processing; omitting it also uses the default tier. Other OpenAI-compatible tier names are not
valid on xAI.

### Reasoning Support

Multiple Grok models support reasoning capabilities:

Grok 4.7 and 4.6: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, high (the default), or xhigh. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort. Reasoning cannot be disabled; Promptfoo rejects none locally.

For Grok 4.7, cap output withmax_completion_tokens for Chat Completions or max_output_tokens for Responses. Chat also accepts max_tokens as an alias; use one spelling throughout an eval, including defaults and test cases. Within test options, set a request option directly or under passthrough, not both. Reasoning effort accepts a direct eval variable such as {{ effort }}; see the optional Grok 4.7 providers in the xAI chat example.

Grok 4.5: Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to low, medium, or high (the default); Promptfoo rejects other values locally. Responses API requests use reasoning.effort with the same values.

Grok 4.3: General-purpose reasoning model. Chat requests can setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high; Responses API requests use reasoning.effort.

Grok Code Fast Models: Thegrok-code-fast-1 family are reasoning models optimized for agentic coding workflows. They support:

- Function calling and tool usage
- Web search viasearch_parameters
- Fast inference with built-in reasoning

### Grok 4.7 Specific Behavior

The xAI release notes list $2/M input, $0.50/M cached input, and $6/M output. At 200K or more input tokens, the rates are $4/M, $1/M, and $12/M respectively. When the API does not return a billed cost, Promptfoo uses these rates, including the 10% premium on xAI's US endpoint; explicit custom rates still take precedence. As with other Grok 4 reasoning models, Promptfoo stripspresence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop.

The Responses API returns encrypted reasoning even wheninclude is omitted. Promptfoo keeps it in response.raw.output; pass these items back unchanged when managing conversation history yourself.

### Grok 4.5 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.5 is an earlier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work:

- 500K context window with text and image input
- Configurable reasoning:reasoning_effort accepts low, medium, or high (defaults to high); none is rejected
- Long-context pricing: requests with at least 200K input tokens use the higher catalog rate ($4/M input, $0.60/M cached input, and $12/M output instead of $2/M, $0.30/M, and $6/M); Promptfoo uses the exact billed ticks when xAI returns them
- Unsupported parameters:presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop are rejected, and Promptfoo strips them automatically
- Ignored parameters: xAI silently ignoreslogprobs and top_logprobs on Grok 4.20 and newer models
- Server-side tools: usexai:responses:grok-4.5 for web search, X search, code execution, and MCP

### Grok 4.3 Specific Behavior

Grok 4.3 is a general-purpose alternative for text workflows:

- Responses API recommended: Usexai:responses:grok-4.3 for server-side tools, multi-turn state, and newer xAI capabilities
- Configurable reasoning: Setreasoning_effort to none, low, medium, or high
- Unsupported parameters: Same restrictions as other Grok 4-family reasoning models (presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, and stop)

cross_cutting.content:
# Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 AI model weights under MIT license

Meituan released the weights for its LongCat-2.5 artificial intelligence model on Nov. 9 under the MIT License, making the vision and coding model available through Hugging Face.

The Chinese food delivery and e-commerce company introduced LongCat-2.5 a week earlier. The model can inspect screenshots and video, examine a codebase, and write or revise software through multiple steps.

Meituan’s API documentation says developers can submit screenshots, charts, images and videos. Images can be embedded in requests or provided by URL, while the video interface uses a URL.

The company highlighted developer demonstrations including a car-launch website by Tasihi, a fantasy game interface by AI Maverick Frank and a shop management website by Aigc Lancet. Meituan also cited an interactive fluid simulation and a 3D exhibition as examples of LongCat-2.5 applications.

Meituan reported that LongCat-2.5 scored 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1, compared with 70.8 for its predecessor. It scored 64.6 on DeepSWE v1.1 versus 9.7, and 58.3 on the SWE Atlas codebase question-answering test versus 33.1.

Its results against proprietary models were mixed. LongCat-2.5 scored 38.5 on Terminal Bench v4.0, while Claude Opus 5 scored 53.9.

Meituan used GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 as proprietary reference models in its launch material. OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol on Sept. 29, while Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 on Sept. 22 and released GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2 on Nov. 9.

Meituan’s rate card lists a limited-time price of $0.006 per million cached input tokens, $0.30 per million uncached input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens. The MIT License permits commercial use, modification and redistribution, subject to notice requirements.

Meituan’s model card says LongCat-2.5 activates about 48 billion parameters per token from 1.6 trillion total parameters. A uniform 16-bit representation of 1.6 trillion parameters would require about 3.2 TB for weights alone, before runtime buffers and context memory.

The Hugging Face repository metadata displays 1.8T parameters, while Meituan’s technical description states 1.6T. Meituan pointed users to an SGLang-FluentLLM deployment guide for neural processing units and described four-bit expert-weight and activation precision on Chinese accelerators.

In October, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security disclosed an order directing federal civilian agencies to exclude DeepSeek from procurement and remove its technology from covered systems, including third-party implementations. The order names DeepSeek and its affiliates.

No publicly disclosed U.S. federal procurement or use restriction specifically named Meituan or LongCat-2.5 as of Nov. 9. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth directed the Pentagon on Feb. 27 to designate Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk to National Security, and formalized that designation on March 3.
