# Changelog

Release announcements and project updates, newest first. Older entries describe support at the time of the announcement; use the current model and deployment guides for current instructions.

## 2026

[2026.10.12] 🔥🔥🔥 We open-source MiniCPM-V 4.7, the first open-source MoE model to run smoothly on-device without compromising performance, setting a new multimodal performance–efficiency Pareto frontier. Try it now!

[2026.06.25] 🔥🔥🔥 MiniCPM-V 4.6 has been merged into Ollama’s official model library, bringing ultra-efficient image and video understanding to local Ollama users. Try it now!

[2026.05.17] ⭐️⭐️⭐️ We release the API service of MiniCPM-V 4.6 and MiniCPM-o 4.5.

[2026.05.11] 🔥🔥🔥 We open-source MiniCPM-V 4.6, with mixed 4x/16x visual token compression. Powered by strong encoding efficiency and its lightweight 1.3B scale, it is our most edge-deployment-friendly model to date, achieving ~1.5x token throughput compared to Qwen3.5 0.8B. Try it now!

[2026.05.07] 📢📢📢 We release the MiniCPM-o 4.5 technical report, introducing the key techniques behind its real-time full-duplex omni-modal interaction. Read it here.

[2026.02.06] 🥳 🥳 🥳 We open-sourced a realtime web demo deployable on your own devices like Mac or GPU. Try it now!

[2026.02.05] 📢📢📢 We note the web demo may experience latency issues due to network conditions. We are working actively to provide a Docker image for local deployment of the real-time interactive Demo as soon as possible. Please stay tuned!

[2026.02.03] 🔥🔥🔥 We open-source MiniCPM-o 4.5, which matches Gemini 2.5 Flash on vision and speech, and supports full-duplex multimodal live streaming. Try it now!

## 2025

[2025.09.18] 📢📢📢 MiniCPM-V 4.5 technical report is now released! See here.

[2025.09.01] ⭐️⭐️⭐️ MiniCPM-V 4.5 has been officially supported by llama.cpp, vLLM, and LLaMA-Factory. You are welcome to use it directly through these official channels! Support for additional frameworks such as Ollama and SGLang is actively in progress.

[2025.08.26] 🔥🔥🔥 We open-source MiniCPM-V 4.5, which outperforms GPT-4o-latest, Gemini-2.0 Pro, and Qwen2.5-VL 72B. It advances popular capabilities of MiniCPM-V, and brings useful new features. Try it now!

[2025.08.02] 🚀🚀🚀 We open-source MiniCPM-V 4.0, which outperforms GPT-4.1-mini-20250414 in image understanding. It advances popular features of MiniCPM-V 2.6, and largely improves the efficiency. We also open-source the iOS App on iPhone and iPad. Try it now!

[2025.08.01] ⭐️⭐️⭐️ We open-sourced the MiniCPM-V & o Cookbook! It provides comprehensive guides for diverse user scenarios, paired with our new Docs Site for smoother onboarding.

[2025.06.20] ⭐️⭐️⭐️ Our official Ollama repository is released. Try our latest models with one click！

[2025.03.01] 🚀🚀🚀 RLAIF-V, the alignment technique of MiniCPM-o, is accepted by CVPR 2025 Highlights！The code, dataset, paper are open-sourced!

[2025.01.24] 📢📢📢 MiniCPM-o 2.6 technical report is released! See here.

[2025.01.23] 💡💡💡 MiniCPM-o 2.6 is now supported by Align-Anything, a framework by PKU-Alignment Team for aligning any-to-any modality large models with human intentions. It supports DPO and SFT fine-tuning on both vision and audio. Try it now!

[2025.01.19] ⭐️⭐️⭐️ MiniCPM-o tops GitHub Trending and reaches top-2 on Hugging Face Trending!

[2025.01.19] 📢 ATTENTION! We are currently working on merging MiniCPM-o 2.6 into the official repositories of llama.cpp, Ollama, and vllm. Until the merge is complete, please USE OUR LOCAL FORKS of llama.cpp, Ollama, and vllm. Using the official repositories before the merge may lead to unexpected issues.

[2025.01.17] We have updated the usage of MiniCPM-o 2.6 int4 quantization version and resolved the model initialization error. Click here and try it now!

[2025.01.13] 🔥🔥🔥 We open-source MiniCPM-o 2.6, which matches GPT-4o-202405 on vision, speech and multimodal live streaming. It advances popular capabilities of MiniCPM-V 2.6, and supports various new fun features. Try it now!

## 2024

[2024.08.17] 🚀🚀🚀 MiniCPM-V 2.6 is now fully supported by official llama.cpp! GGUF models of various sizes are available here.

[2024.08.15] We now also support multi-image SFT. For more details, please refer to the document.

[2024.08.14] MiniCPM-V 2.6 now also supports fine-tuning with the SWIFT framework!

[2024.08.10] 🚀🚀🚀 MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 is now fully supported by official llama.cpp! GGUF models of various sizes are available here.

[2024.08.06] 🔥🔥🔥 We open-source MiniCPM-V 2.6, which outperforms GPT-4V on single image, multi-image and video understanding. It advances popular features of MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5, and can support real-time video understanding on iPad. Try it now!

[2024.08.03] MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 technical report is released! See here.

[2024.07.19] MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 supports vLLM now! See here.

[2024.06.03] Now, you can run MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 on multiple low VRAM GPUs(12 GB or 16 GB) by distributing the model's layers across multiple GPUs. For more details, check this link.

[2024.05.28] 🚀🚀🚀 MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 now fully supports its feature in llama.cpp and Ollama! Please pull the latest code of our provided forks (llama.cpp, Ollama). GGUF models in various sizes are available here. MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 series is not supported by the official repositories yet, and we are working hard to merge PRs. Please stay tuned!

[2024.05.28] 💫 We now support LoRA fine-tuning for MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5, using only 2 V100 GPUs! See more statistics here.

[2024.05.25] MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 now supports streaming outputs and customized system prompts. Try it here!

[2024.05.24] We release the MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5 gguf, which supports llama.cpp inference and provides a 6~8 token/s smooth decoding on mobile phones. Try it now!

[2024.05.23] 🔥🔥🔥 MiniCPM-V tops GitHub Trending and Hugging Face Trending! Our demo, recommended by Hugging Face Gradio’s official account, is available here. Come and try it out!

[2024.05.23] 🔍 We've released a comprehensive comparison between Phi-3-vision-128k-instruct and MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5, including benchmark evaluations, multilingual capabilities, and inference efficiency 🌟📊🌍🚀. Click here to view more details.

[2024.05.20] We open-soure MiniCPM-Llama3-V 2.5, it has improved OCR capability and supports 30+ languages, representing the first end-side MLLM achieving GPT-4V level performance! We provide efficient inference and simple fine-tuning. Try it now!

[2024.04.23] MiniCPM-V-2.0 supports vLLM now! Click here to view more details.

[2024.04.18] We create a HuggingFace Space to host the demo of MiniCPM-V 2.0 at here!

[2024.04.17] MiniCPM-V-2.0 supports deploying WebUI Demo now!

[2024.04.15] MiniCPM-V-2.0 now also supports fine-tuning with the SWIFT framework, with streaming inference enabled!

[2024.04.12] We open-source MiniCPM-V 2.0, which achieves comparable performance with Gemini Pro in understanding scene text and outperforms strong Qwen-VL-Chat 9.6B and Yi-VL 34B on OpenCompass, a comprehensive evaluation over 11 popular benchmarks. Click here to view the MiniCPM-V 2.0 technical blog.

[2024.03.14] MiniCPM-V now supports fine-tuning with the SWIFT framework. Thanks to Jintao for the contribution！

[2024.03.01] MiniCPM-V can now be deployed on Mac!

[2024.02.01] We open-source MiniCPM-V and OmniLMM-12B, which support efficient end-side deployment and powerful multimodal capabilities correspondingly.

# Inkling 2 Small from Thinking Machines Lab Is Now Available in Snowflake Cortex Training

Enterprises are increasingly turning to customizing open-weight models on their own data and context to have full control over the behavior and results.

Today, we are excited to share that Inkling 2 Small, the latest open-weight model from Thinking Machines Lab, is now available in Snowflake Cortex Training (public preview). Teams can start benchmarking, post-training, evaluating and serving Inkling 2 Small on their own enterprise workloads today, directly where their data lives and governed by the same controls they already rely on.

## What is Inkling 2 Small?

Inkling 2 Small is the second model generation from Thinking Machines Lab. It is a Mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 594 billion total parameters and 17 billion active parameters, and it supports image inputs and variable reasoning effort.

Inkling 2 Small is built for long-horizon agentic work. Thinking Machines Lab trained it with reinforcement learning (RL) on hundreds of thousands of long-horizon coding tasks across multiple agent harnesses, and it reports that the model follows instructions more closely, considers changes carefully and verifies its own work without being asked. That makes it easier to use inside real agent loops, and it shows in its coding results, including 86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 (Hard) and 72.1% on DeepSWE v1.1.

The model is also multimodal. Image inputs let it incorporate visual feedback, for example to iteratively build and refine interfaces and designs. And because only 17 billion of its parameters are active per token, the MoE architecture delivers high capability at a lower inference cost than a dense model of comparable size. With weights released under the Apache 2.0 license today, enterprises keep full ownership of the models they customize.

## What can you do with Inkling 2 Small on Snowflake?

Cortex Training, Snowflake’s serverless offering for customizing and deploying open-weight LLMs, is designed to make open-weight model customization simple, flexible and cost efficient. We are thrilled to welcome the Inkling family of models to Cortex Training’s rich catalog of existing open-weight models, including families such as Qwen, GLM, Nemotron, Gemma and DeepSeek. Inkling 2 Small is available for both post-training and inference today.

# Klook launches K.ai, an AI agent that manages merchants' back-office operations

November 12, 2026 11:11 GMT+700

Klook launches AI agent that manages merchants’ back-office operations

K.ai goes beyond answering questions to executing inventory, pricing, and booking-related tasks in Klook's merchant portal

Singapore and Hong Kong (ANTARA/PRNewswire)- Klook, a leading global platform for experiences, launches K.ai, an AI agent that helps experiences merchants manage their businesses by executing everyday tasks in Klook's merchant portal.

Unlike conventional AI assistants that only answer questions or provide recommendations, K.ai can retrieve business information and act on merchants' instructions, from checking bookings and availability to updating inventory and pricing. This reduces the need for merchants to navigate multiple menus and complete routine tasks manually.

K.ai is now being introduced to Klook's merchants through a phased global rollout, ahead of the year-end travel season.

Bringing SMEs from offline to AI-powered operations

Experiences remain one of travel's least digitized categories. According to Euromonitor, only about 34% of experiences bookings are made online, compared with 66% for accommodations and 81% for flights.

A key reason is fragmentation: small and medium-sized (SME) operators make up around 95% of the sector, and many lack the digital reach to sell beyond walk-ins and offline channels. The result is a large, fragmented supply base that travelers still struggle to find, compare and book online.

By bringing these merchants online, Klook makes them discoverable and bookable to travelers worldwide, and by embedding AI into Klook's existing tech infrastructure, it helps them leapfrog from manual processes to AI-powered business management.

"Many experiences merchants don't have dedicated teams to manage technology or back-office operations. With K.ai, we're bringing the most practical and valuable agentic AI capabilities into their day-to-day operations, removing much of the manual work involved in running their businesses, so they can spend more time on what they do best: delivering meaningful experiences for travelers," says Bernie Xiong, Co-founder and CTO of Klook.

From answering questions to getting work done

For SME merchants, managing bookings, inventory and pricing is essential but time-consuming. While most AI business assistants only answer questions, K.ai goes further — it answers questions and takes action.

A merchant can ask, "What did my bookings look like last week?" and receive a report. The merchant can then instruct K.ai to "Raise the weekend price by 10%" and have the change applied in the merchant portal.

Early results from merchants using K.ai demonstrate operational improvements. Tasks that required multiple steps can now be completed 95% faster for individual inventory and pricing updates, and 97% faster for batch checks of products, inventory and orders.

Beyond efficiency, merchants using K.ai recorded 3.4 times as many monthly bookings of those not using the agent. With the ability to adjust operational details in seconds, merchants are better equipped to respond to changing demand and capture booking opportunities.

"I used to block out an hour every morning to update prices and availability across my tours," says Erica Yu, Co-founder of MyProGuide in Taiwan. "The difference is tangible. Now I tell K.ai what I want, and it's done before my coffee is. I'm catching last-minute demand that I used to miss, and I finally have more time to work on the tours themselves."

From back-office operations to business growth

Beyond supporting day-to-day merchant portal operations and queries, K.ai also simplifies other time-consuming aspects of running an experiences business.

With one-click product listing, merchants can upload existing materials and have K.ai generate structured product listings, pre-filling fields for merchants to review and edit instead of building listings from scratch.

K.ai also helps merchants make more informed business decisions by turning customer reviews and performance data into actionable insights.

Through the Reviews and Dashboard pages, K.ai highlights changes in business performance, identifies potential reasons behind them and surfaces opportunities for improvement. This helps merchants better understand customer needs, improve service quality and refine their offerings, shifting their focus from routine administration to growing their businesses.

# Databricks unveils new version of AI agent Genie

## AI Summary Databricks on Nov. 11 unveiled a new version of its AI agent, Genie. TechCrunch reported that the updated tool can support multi-step work that takes a long time. Databricks built an ontology to provide Genie with context from information customers store on the platform. CEO Ali Ghodsi showed his own agent with recent conversations and charts, and said he uses it to surface issues hard to hear at the top.

- Writer Chi-gyu Hwang
- published 2026-11-12 14:52:09
- updated 2026-11-12 14:53:09

Databricks said on Nov. 11 it has unveiled a new version of its AI agent, Genie.

TechCrunch reported that Genie supports multi-step tasks that take a long time to complete.

Databricks also built an ontology to provide Genie with context from information customers store on the Databricks platform.

The company said executives can assign Genie a range of tasks and it can finish them without human supervision.

Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi (알리 고드시) opened the agent he actually uses instead of giving a product demo, showing recent conversations and charts.

Genie analysed low-scoring items in an employee satisfaction survey. It also supported evaluating and filtering improvement proposals from some executives. It summarised how a large sales proposal to a potential customer failed. The summary included features the customer demanded as purchase conditions. TechCrunch reported that Genie also reviewed past broadcasts featuring Ghodsi and generated expected questions for a podcast interview.

Ghodsi said he uses Genie to find things that are hard to hear from the CEO seat. He described it as a channel for hearing unvarnished accounts of what is not going well at the company.

At a small startup, a CEO knows all employees and staff can relay bad news immediately, but Databricks has 12,000 employees. At that scale, failures in the sales field are difficult to reach the CEO.

Ghodsi said, "There are many companies with more than 150 employees," and added, "Many people can get value from Genie."

Databricks is pitching Genie as an always-on agent for executives. Ghodsi said he also uses Genie in his personal life instead of OpenClaw, Instinct and Muse, which he said have questionable security. He said Genie can play the role in business that AI, agents and harnesses play for programmers.

On concerns that agents could increase corporate AI costs, he said, "You can control it with Unity Gateway," adding, "Companies can set usage limits with this product and switch to cheaper open-weight models."

# Databricks launches always-on Genie AI agent for firms
Thu, 12th Nov 2026 (Today) 
SEAN MITCHELL Publisher

Databricks has launched the second generation of Genie, positioning it as an always-on autonomous AI agent for enterprise work. The update expands its push to embed AI agents in existing corporate data and software environments.

The new version is designed to run continuously in the background and handle longer-running tasks without repeated user prompts. Workers can assign a goal, set boundaries, and let the system track progress, follow up on missing inputs, and return when a person needs to make a decision.

The launch also includes Genie Search, intended to give staff and software agents a single governed search layer across structured and unstructured information, and new features in Genie Ontology, Databricks' framework for capturing business definitions, metrics, reporting lines, and processes.

The product operates within a customer's existing Databricks environment and remains subject to security, permissions, and approval controls already set through Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway. Every action is auditable.

Databricks is targeting a common point of tension in the adoption of AI agents by large organisations. While many companies are experimenting with tools that can answer questions or complete tasks, concerns remain about giving those systems access to financial planning data, customer records, and internal documents.

Under the new model, Genie can be used for operational work such as monitoring quarterly forecasts, tracking revenue trends, analysing employee survey responses, and identifying changes in customer usage patterns. The system can delegate work to sub-agents, present outstanding issues in a priority inbox, and send email alerts when user input is required.

Search layer

Genie Search extends the product beyond the Databricks lakehouse to business applications including Google Drive, Jira, and Confluence. Teams can either index content where it already sits, ingest it through Lakeflow Connect, or query applications live through MCP.

Databricks now offers more than 100 connectors to support those approaches. Instead of searching each application separately, users and agents can search once across multiple sources, reducing tool calls and token usage, according to the company.

That search function is tied to Genie Ontology, which Databricks describes as a way to maintain an up-to-date understanding of how a company defines its data and how its people and processes fit together. The latest release adds support for business logic from external business intelligence tools and introduces an organisational structure connector.

Databricks also introduced Ontology Manager, a new interface for teams to manage and govern business context. The tool can recommend areas for refinement by flagging concepts that are frequently queried.

Broader access

Another part of the update is wider distribution of Genie across third-party AI and workplace tools. Users will be able to access Genie through a web browser, mobile app, email, and collaboration and AI products including ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, and Grok Bot.

The release also broadens the content Genie agents can work with. Agents can now operate across PDFs, contracts, and slide decks in Unity Catalog volumes alongside governed tables, without the need for a separate vector index.

Databricks is also adding dynamic slides, dashboards, and interactive reports that remain tied to governed data and update as that data changes.

Ali Ghodsi, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Databricks, said the product is already changing how he works. "Genie has made me a 10x more productive CEO, and now it doesn't wait for me to ask," Ghodsi said. "Every day, Genie keeps up with my inbox, preps me for meetings, and runs in the background, coming back only when it needs a decision. It can do that because it knows how our company works: what we mean by revenue, which numbers are official, and who can see what. That's the power of horizontal context, and Genie delivers it."

Partners and customers also described governed business context as central to adoption. "Teams make their best decisions when trusted context shows up in the flow of work. With Genie Agents now connected to Slack, sales, finance, and operations teams can go from question to action without leaving the conversation. We're thrilled to work alongside Databricks to bring governed, reliable insights to where the work happens," said Jaime DeLanghe, Chief Product Officer of Slack.

Headspace pointed to the role of agreed definitions in reducing ambiguity in AI outputs. "AI is only as good as the definitions behind it, so we built our Genie Agents on agreed, governed definitions, and now every answer matches. We expanded self-service analytics by putting plain-language access to our data in the hands of teams across the business, not just analysts, so people can act on numbers they trust," said Marlissa Wong, Director of Data Engineering at Headspace.

HelloFresh cited a measurable effect on advertising decisions. "With Genie constantly analysing performance signals, we've improved programmatic ad ROI and reduced the time to identify ad winners on Meta by 75%. Unity Gateway gives us the flexibility to use the best model for each job without managing separate integrations," said Alan Khalil, Associate Director of Data Science and Engineering at HelloFresh.

Databricks said Genie and Genie Ontology are generally available, while Genie Search, Ontology Manager, and the always-on version of Genie are being rolled out through preview and beta programmes.

cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief Australia - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Simpro launches JustDo AI agent for trade businesses
Thu, 12th Nov 2026 (Today) 
KAREN JOY BACUDO Finance Editor

Simpro Group has launched JustDo, an AI operations agent for trade businesses, across Simpro, AroFlo and BigChange in the US, Australia and the UK.

Designed to handle office administration tasks within the company's field service management software, JustDo can work on customer, quote and job-related tasks. Staff can submit requests in plain English by typing, speaking, or attaching materials such as emails, photos, PDFs or spreadsheets. The system then checks records, prepares draft entries and shows a preview before anything is saved.

The launch comes as trade businesses face pressure to keep up with demand while managing skilled labour shortages and tight margins. Many firms still rely on staff to manually copy information into scheduling and job systems before work can be booked.

Simpro's internal benchmark puts administration at about 18.5 hours a week per business. Average net margins in the sector are about 6%, it said, which can make it difficult for smaller operators to add office staff.

JustDo is being positioned as a way to reduce that workload rather than replace employees. The software is intended to help existing office teams process more work and move jobs to the schedule more quickly.

Admin tasks

The product can turn an emailed repair request into a draft job, check whether the customer already exists in the system and prepare records for review. It can also start a quote from an email, PDF or short text instruction, setting out line items before a staff member approves the entry.

Other functions include creating tasks in bulk, raising purchase orders for jobs that need materials, flagging and archiving inactive customers, and checking completed job cards before they are sent to customers. The system works within a business's own records through platform application programming interfaces and follows each user's existing permissions.

There is no separate tool for customers to connect or maintain, and the product does not replace the underlying field service management system. Every action is previewed, while more sensitive or harder-to-reverse actions require approval.

A side panel shows users what the software is doing and why. Simpro said that design choice reflects concerns among trade businesses about mistakes that could affect customers.

In State of the Trades 2026, a YouGov survey in the UK cited by Simpro, 30% of respondents said customer-affecting errors were their main concern about AI. That helps explain why suppliers in the sector are emphasising review and approval steps rather than full automation.

Market focus

The rollout covers customers using Simpro Lightning, BigChange Lightning and AroFlo Lightning. Simpro Group said the product runs on a credit-based model and is still being developed, with additional features being added in response to customer requests.

Simpro Group serves more than 24,000 trade businesses and 450,000 users across the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom through Simpro, AroFlo, BigChange and ClockShark. Its software is used by contractors and service firms to manage scheduling, dispatch, quoting, invoicing and workforce management.

The launch of an AI assistant focused on office administration reflects a broader push by software suppliers to move beyond generic chat tools into systems that can carry out operational tasks in context. In field service, that means tying requests directly to schedules, job records, customer histories and invoicing workflows.

That approach could be particularly relevant for small and mid-sized contractors, which often lack dedicated back-office teams. By reducing manual re-entry and routine checking, software vendors are trying to give those businesses some of the administrative support that larger national operators can afford to build in-house.

"The trades can't hire fast enough to meet demand, and every hour a technician or owner spends on paperwork is an hour not spent on a job. Just Do gives those hours back, so contractors can take on more work and grow without adding headcount. It also gives the small and mid-sized shops that make up most of the industry back-office support that used to be available only to the biggest national players," aid Fred Voccola, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Simpro Group.

# New Relic launches AI agent to automate Kubernetes incident detection and resolution

The agent can automatically identify the root causes of infrastructure incidents and generate remediation code for engineers to review and execute.

New Relic has launched an AI-powered agent designed to help engineering teams identify and resolve issues in complex Kubernetes environments. The New Relic Autopilot Kubernetes Agent is designed for site reliability engineers (SREs) and platform engineers.

It can automatically identify the root causes of infrastructure incidents and generate remediation code for engineers to review and execute.

New Relic said its agent runs more than 90 specialised diagnostic detectors across Kubernetes events, object descriptions, logs and application performance monitoring (APM) traces. It uses the company's Ground Truth context engine to analyse operational data and identify the underlying causes of incidents.

The system can diagnose issues including resource constraints, scheduling failures, network errors and cloud misconfigurations. It also generates context-aware remediation code, allowing engineers to address problems without spending hours analysing multiple dashboards or relying on generic AI-generated recommendations.

"The New Relic Autopilot Kubernetes Agent embeds specialised, agentic AI directly into the engineer's containerised workflows to eliminate the guesswork from complex cluster incidents while keeping the engineer safely in control. Because it works natively across any telemetry source, it provides a level of full-stack observability that specialised or closed-system tools cannot match,” said Brian Emerson, Chief Product Officer, New Relic.

# CNCF Welcomes Vultr as a Platinum Member to Advance Open and Sovereign Cloud Infrastructure for AI

Upgrade extends Vultr’s 5-year history with CNCF and expands its voice in shaping open interoperability for AI factory infrastructure at global scale

Key Highlights

- Vultr has upgraded to a CNCF Platinum membership, expanding its role in shaping open interoperability for AI infrastructure.
- Vultr contributed both CPU + GPU infrastructure capacity support for CNCF project testing
- Vultr launched the Vultr Open Source Alliance, connecting its CNCF partnership to a broader commitment across open infrastructure, cloud native technologies, and AI tooling.

KUBECON + CLOUDNATIVECON NORTH AMERICA, SALT LAKE CITY – November 10, 2026– The Cloud Native Computing Foundation® (CNCF®), which builds sustainable ecosystems for cloud native software, today announced that Vultr has upgraded its CNCF membership to Platinum at a critical moment when cloud native and AI infrastructure are converging on shared, open interoperability.

This upgrade builds on Vultr deepening its partnerships with CNCF projects to help drive developer adoption of open, composable infrastructure through the newly launched Vultr Open Source Alliance. The alliance brings together work across open infrastructure, cloud native technologies, AI, and developer ecosystems. Together, these efforts reflect a simple principle: developers should be able to choose the infrastructure, frameworks, models, tools, and protocols that fit their workloads without being locked into a single technology stack.

“AI factory infrastructure should be open and fungible, not another walled garden,” said Chris Aniszczyk, CTO, CNCF. “Platinum membership in CNCF is a real commitment to help build that open future and we’re glad to have Vultr at the table as we figure out what composable AI infrastructure looks like for the next decade.”

Building on a foundation started in 2021 when Vultr first joined CNCF as a Silver Member, recent milestones underscore Vultr’s growing footprint in cloud native AI infrastructure. Vultr’s engineering team has worked directly with maintainers on CNCF projects including Kubernetes and Kubeflow, contributing feedback and improvements upstream rather than only consuming the technology downstream. Its Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE) is a CNCF Certified Kubernetes product. Vultr runs heterogeneous GPU and CPU infrastructure that supports open source frameworks including PyTorch for model training and Kubernetes for inference, and recently contributed both CPU and GPU infrastructure capacity support for CNCF project testing. Vultr is also a member of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a separate Linux Foundation initiative stewarding open standards for the agentic AI stack.

“Open source is the foundation of modern AI infrastructure, and the developer community should be free to choose the frameworks, models, and infrastructure that fit their workloads, without being locked into a single stack or cloud,” said Kevin Cochrane, Chief Marketing Officer of Vultr. “Moving to Platinum membership builds on five years of working alongside the CNCF community. Through the Vultr Open Source Alliance and our CPU and GPU contributions to CNCF project testing, we’re helping build the open, interoperable, and sovereign AI infrastructure that the next generation of applications will depend on.”

To learn more about becoming a CNCF member, visit https://www.cncf.io/about/join/.

About Cloud Native Computing Foundation

Cloud native computing empowers organizations to build and run scalable applications with an open source software stack in public, private, and hybrid clouds. The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) hosts critical components of the global technology infrastructure, including Kubernetes, Prometheus, and Envoy. CNCF brings together the industry’s top developers, end users, and vendors and runs the largest open source developer conferences in the world. Supported by nearly 800 members, including the world’s largest cloud computing and software companies, as well as over 200 innovative startups, CNCF is part of the nonprofit Linux Foundation. For more information, please visit www.cncf.io.

# [PRNewswire] Gcore and TengriAI to explore 100 MW AI data center

Press Releases 09:04 November 13, 2026

-- Phased project would give Central Asia large-scale GPU capacity run in the region

LUXEMBOURG and ASTANA, Kazakhstan Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- Gcore and TengriAI have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to explore a GPU data center in Kazakhstan with a target capacity of up to 100 MW, phased between 2027 and 2029.

Central Asia has little domestic AI compute, so organizations depend on capacity in Europe, the Gulf or East Asia, often outside regulatory jurisdiction.

"Every market we work in is asking the same question: how do we run AI on our own terms?" says Andre Reitenbach, CEO of Gcore. "The project would put large-scale GPU infrastructure in the country, operated from the country, for customers across the region."

The platform is the one Gcore runs in its own GPU clouds as an NVIDIA Preferred Cloud Partner. Customers could meter, bill and resell capacity, or run isolated workloads that never leave the facility.

"Our goal is to make Kazakhstan a leading AI token hub in Central Asia," said Nurassyl Medeu, General Director of TengriAI. "Gcore operates GPU clouds at scale and has done this with telecom operators."

Gcore is one of few Europe-headquartered companies that operates its own GPU clouds, owns the global network and secures every deployment. "Software vendors have never operated a platform. Hyperscalers will not hand over the keys. We do both," said Reitenbach.

Kazakhstan offers competitively priced energy, available land, lower cooling costs and a government that treats AI infrastructure as a national priority. Its location and the Astana International Financial Centre's common-law framework make it a natural base for neighboring markets.

# Rackspace signs capacity agreements with Together AI and Blacksmith

Deployment planned for 2027

Rackspace has signed two customer agreements for compute capacity.

The first agreement is with neocloud startup Together AI and is a multi-year AI infrastructure agreement under which Rackspace will provide and operate dedicated Nvidia GB300 NVL72 infrastructure for Together AI.

Deployment is planned for 2027. Rackspace will also operate the associated power, liquid cooling, networking, and storage.

“Enterprise AI requires more than access to compute. Success depends on bringing compute into production, operating it reliably and delivering sustained value. That requires deep infrastructure and engineering expertise combined with operational accountability,” said Gajen Kandiah, CEO of Rackspace. “Rackspace brings more than 25 years of experience operating complex enterprise environments. Today’s announcement provides an opportunity to apply that experience to the dedicated infrastructure supporting Together AI’s inference platform.”

The companies also entered into a separate, non-binding letter of intent (LOI) to explore a joint go-to-market approach for enterprise-focused AI solutions, with Together AI providing inference capabilities and Rackspace providing the supporting AI infrastructure.

"Scaling in the enterprise requires infrastructure that can grow with our ambitions while delivering the performance and reliability customers expect," added Vipul Ved Prakash, founder and CEO of Together AI. "Rackspace brings the infrastructure engineering and operational expertise to support that growth, and we look forward to exploring additional opportunities together."

How much capacity Rackspace is providing to Together AI has not been shared, nor has the data center it will be deployed in, beyond that it is a "purpose-built, liquid-cooled facility, supported by Nvidia networking."

The second contract is with Blacksmith, an infrastructure platform for building and testing code.

Another multi-year agreement, Rackspace will provide Blacksmith with dedicated compute powered by AMD Epyc CPUs along with storage, totaling approximately 2MW of capacity located in Northern Virginia. Rackspace operates a data center in Ashburn, Virginia. Deployment will begin in early 2027.

“When we talk to developers and engineering teams, we keep hearing that AI is making it much easier to write code, but getting those changes tested and ready to ship is becoming the bottleneck. We’re building Blacksmith to help developers merge code faster and feel confident about what they’re shipping. Our partnership with Rackspace will help us scale the infrastructure behind that work,” said Aditya “JP” Jayaprakash, co-founder and CEO of Blacksmith.

Rackspace has an existing agreement with AMD to deploy 30MW of dedicated AMD compute across its data centers through 2028.

In addition to the customer contracts, this month Rackspace entered into a share purchase agreement with an investor group led by Voss Capital, LP, providing for an aggregate $66 million private placement of Rackspace common stock.

The company will use the funding for general corporate purposes, working capital, capital expenditures, and growth capital, including funding for GPU-related initiatives. Rackspace said it expects to seek separate financing for the purchase of the Nvidia GB300 NVL72 systems for Together AI and is in active discussions with potential lenders; however, no definitive GPU financing commitment has been obtained as of the time of writing.
